Third, the debris: small embers detach from the burn line and rise, each one a tiny hard point of orange light with a faint trailing glow, varying in brightness and size, drifting apart rather than travelling in a line, some already fading to dark. Alongside them float small dark flakes of ash and torn paper fragments, tumbling at different angles. Nothing about the burn is symmetrical or regular: the flame is not a neat cone, the char line is not a straight edge, and the embers are not evenly spaced.

LIGHTING — Three sources. The first is the fire itself, low and central, close to the chest and below the face: it is small, hard and warm, and it lights everything from beneath, so the underside of the chin, the front of the throat, the inside of the collar, the lower lip, the underside of the nose and the fingers holding the note are all lit from below with crisp shadow edges that run upward, and the eye sockets and the underside of the brow ridge stay in shadow. It is the brightest light on the face and it flickers, so its intensity varies across surfaces rather than falling evenly. The second is a magenta-violet source placed high and to camera left and behind, which rims the top of the hair, the near cheekbone and the near shoulder with a coloured edge that varies in width and breaks where the form turns away. The third is a weak violet fill from camera right that opens the shadow side just enough to keep it readable. The face sits about a stop below the flame's core. The suit takes very little of any of them and sits three stops below the face. The background is about two stops below the lit skin. Every transition curves with the surface it crosses; nothing is straight-edged. The lighting sets brightness and falloff only.

BACKGROUND — A dark interior space, out of focus and without any identifiable object, structure or edge: a broad wall of mottled violet and deep purple, uneven and blotchy in tone, with a soft brighter pool behind the head and the corners falling away dark. Drifting through it, four or five loose banknotes at different distances and different angles — some nearly edge-on, some flat, each curling slightly, each rendered at a different degree of softness according to how far away it is, and none of them repeating another's angle. Among them, scattered dark flakes of confetti and paper, and a field of small orange embers spread irregularly through the depth, clustering in places and absent in others. Depth is carried by four separations: the burning note and the hand nearest the lens, the person, the drifting banknotes at mid-distance, and the wall far behind.

FOCUS — Depth-of-field blur only, no motion blur anywhere; every edge is a still edge and the flame is frozen rather than smeared. Critical sharpness sits on the eyes, seen through the clear lenses, and on the bridge of the nose — the lashes, the iris texture and the skin texture across the cheekbone are all resolved — together with the rim of the spectacle frame. The plane of sharpness carries the whole face and the collar. The burning note and the holding hand, being closer to the lens, are slightly softer, the paper's line-work and the knuckle skin still fully readable. The flame is soft by its own nature. The drifting banknotes are well outside the plane and clearly out of focus, softer the further back they sit. The embers nearest the lens render as small soft glowing discs and those further back as tiny sharp points. The wall is dissolved completely.

COLOUR — Two families in opposition. Cool: the violet and deep purple of the entire background, the coloured rim on the hair and the near cheek, and the shadow side of the suit, which keeps its navy and never goes black or grey. Warm: the flame, the embers, and everything the fire touches — the underside of the chin, the throat, the collar's inner edge and the fingers. The banknotes are a pale desaturated grey-green and are the only near-neutral objects in the frame; the shirt is neutral white. The skin keeps whatever tone image 1 has: warmed and pushed golden on the lower face and the hand where the fire reaches, cooled toward violet on the upper sides and the temples, and still clearly reading as skin in both zones — it must not be recoloured into a single flat purple or a single flat orange. There is no green anywhere except in the notes.

CAPTURE — A real exposure made on a full-frame camera. Light falls off strongly toward the four corners. The core of the flame and the brightest embers clip hard to white and bloom slightly into the darkness around them; the lit underside of the chin and the white collar clip softly and keep their modelling. Shadows stay open and slightly lifted — the navy suit holds its weave and its colour rather than collapsing to black, and the darkest corner of the background sits above pure black. Render the skin as a real camera renders skin, whatever skin image 1 provides: pores and fine surface texture resolved at the plane of sharpness, individual hairs at the hairline and brows resolved, tone varying across the face rather than running uniform, and a slight specular sheen on the high points of the forehead, the nose and the cheekbones. Do not smooth, retouch, even out or plasticise it, and do not add or subtract any feature. Visible fine grain throughout, heavier in the dark background.

FINAL CHECK — One person, alone, dead-on frontal and symmetrical, the head about half the frame height and centred, the eyes on the lens and the face completely unreacting. A hundred-dollar bill held at a diagonal across the lower centre of the frame between fingertips, burning at its upper end with a ragged char line and a leaning flame that lights the face from below. Banknotes and embers drift out of focus in a violet background. The face, skin, hair and any facial hair are exactly as image 1 shows them and nothing about them has been invented. Do not widen the shot and do not make the face react.

title: Leonardo DiCaprio em Retrato Vibrante com Óculos
description: Um retrato de Leonardo DiCaprio usando óculos, com iluminação vibrante em tons de roxo e rosa, criando um clima moderno.
prompt:
SWAP SLOT — Image 1 is the identity reference. Take from it only the face, the skin tone, the hair colour and texture, and the head and body proportions of the person in this picture. Take nothing else from it: not the clothing, not the eyewear, not the pose, not the expression, not the framing, not the lighting, not the background, not the colour palette, not the mood. Everything else in this picture is built from the text below. If image 1 shows different clothes or a different setting, ignore them completely.

THE PICTURE — A vertical bust portrait of one adult man, alone, in a plain black crew-neck sweatshirt and clear transparent glasses, his head level and his eyes looking off past the camera to the upper right, against a saturated magenta-to-violet backdrop.

THE READING — This is a quiet, considered portrait, and the quiet is produced by physical facts rather than by mood. He is not looking at the lens: his eyes are aimed off past it and slightly up, so the viewer is watching him think rather than being addressed. His face is doing nothing at all — no smile, no frown, no set jaw — and that stillness is the point; any expression would make it a different picture. He wears a plain black sweatshirt with no collar, no tailoring, no jewellery and no object of any kind, so nothing in the wardrobe asks to be read and the whole frame reduces to a head. His glasses are transparent rather than tinted, so the eyes stay fully visible and nothing is hidden. And the drama is entirely in the background: the colour is saturated and the light is soft, so the picture is intense without the man having to perform anything.

FRAMING AND CAMERA — Aspect ratio 4:5, vertical. Single subject, bust length. The top edge of the frame sits about one tenth of the frame height above the crown of his hair. His head, from the top of the hair to the point of the chin, measures a little under half the frame height, so it is large and close. It is centred just left of the middle of the frame, at about forty-eight hundredths of the frame width. The bottom edge of the frame crosses his chest well below the neckline, so the black sweatshirt fills the lower third of the picture as one broad dark mass. His shoulders run almost the full width of the frame, and the left and right edges each cross the top of a shoulder, both continuing past those edges. Lens 85mm, camera at his eye level, held perfectly level with no tilt. Aperture f/2.8.

POSE — He stands upright, shoulders square to the lens and level, held down and relaxed, weight even with no hip shift. His torso is rotated only about ten degrees toward camera left. His head is upright and level — not tilted back, not tucked — and turned about fifteen degrees toward camera left, so the face is off-frontal and the far cheek narrows slightly. His eyes are aimed up and to the right of the lens at a point outside the frame, the irises sitting a little high and toward the outer corner of each eye so a band of white shows on the inner side of each. Both arms hang down at his sides in an unbroken line from shoulder to upper arm, and both continue past the left and right edges of the frame. The neck is relaxed and the shoulders carry no lift.

EXPRESSION — The brows sit level and untensed, with no furrow between them and only two faint settled horizontal lines across the forehead. The upper eyelids are open and steady and the lower lids relaxed, the eyes held on their distant point without narrowing. The nostrils are relaxed. The lips are closed and lightly together, full and unpressed, the corners level with the faintest downward set. The jaw is loose and unclenched. The cheeks are completely still. Every muscle in the face is released; nothing is being done with it.

HAIR — The hair from image 1, worn medium length and combed back and slightly to one side off the forehead, lying close to the skull with the comb tracks visible as fine parallel grooves running back over the crown, thinning a little at the temples, and with several loose strands breaking free at the crown and along the front hairline. Because a strong coloured light sits behind him, those free strands are lit from behind and read as bright coloured filaments against the backdrop. A short irregular stubble across the jaw, the chin and the upper lip, patchy rather than even — denser at the chin and along the jawline and sparse across the cheek, with individual hairs and the bare skin between them both clearly visible, and a scattering of paler hairs mixed unevenly through the darker ones.

WARDROBE — A plain black crew-neck sweatshirt in a heavyweight brushed cotton. The nap is matte and slightly fuzzy, so it scatters almost all the light and reads as the deepest, flattest black in the frame, showing form only as a faint lift toward grey along the crest of each shoulder and along the top of the neckband. The neckband is a ribbed knit that sits close to the throat: each raised rib takes a thin line of light on its crest and goes dark in the channel between, and it is the one place on the garment with visible structure. The shoulder seam and a soft fold across the upper chest are the only other lines in it. A few pale lint fibres cling to the shoulder and catch the light as tiny bright specks. No print, no logo, no pattern, no collar, no jewellery.

PROPS AND OBJECTS — Glasses with clear transparent acetate frames, rounded rectangular in shape with fairly thick rims, straight temple arms and small metal rivets at the hinges. The acetate is translucent, not white and not grey, and that is the whole behaviour of the material: light enters the plastic and travels through it, so the frame glows faintly along its thicker edges, the skin of the temple and cheekbone is visible through the frame slightly softened and shifted where it passes behind, and the rim reads as a bright clear outline rather than a solid band. The hinge rivets return two tiny hard pinpoints. The lenses are clear and untinted — the eyes, lashes and lower brows are fully visible through them — and each lens carries a broad soft pale blue-white reflection across its upper portion, larger and brighter on the far lens than on the near one, spread smoothly rather than sharply edged, and never covering the eye beneath it.

LIGHTING — Two sources. The key is a large soft neutral source placed forward and to camera right, a little above his eye level: it lays a broad graduated pass across the forehead, the ridge of the nose, the near cheekbone and the near side of the jaw, with soft-cored shadow edges — a wide band under the brow, a short soft shadow from the nose onto the upper lip, a soft shadow under the lower lip and under the chin onto the throat. The second is the backdrop's own coloured light, placed behind him and to camera left: it spills forward around the far side of the head, laying a saturated coloured wash down the far cheek, along the far jaw and across the far ear, which is thin enough that light passes through it and it glows from within. That coloured side sits about a stop and a half below the key side. The shadow between the two stays open and readable. The black sweatshirt takes almost nothing and sits four stops below the face. The backdrop is brightest in a broad pool behind and to the right of his head, about half a stop above the lit side of his face, and falls off toward the top corners, the left edge and the bottom, ending about two and a half stops down. Every transition curves with the surface it crosses; nothing is straight-edged. The lighting sets brightness and falloff only.

BACKGROUND — A plain seamless studio backdrop, unbroken, with no seam, texture, object, edge or shadow anywhere on it, its surface matte and paper-like. It carries a single continuous colour gradient: a bright saturated magenta-pink in the pool behind and to the right of his head, deepening outward through violet to a dark blue-purple at the top corners, along the left edge and across the bottom. The gradient must be perfectly smooth, with no banding, no stepping and no visible edge between one tone and the next. Depth comes from that gradient alone.

FOCUS — Depth-of-field blur only, no motion blur anywhere; every edge in the picture is a still edge. Critical sharpness sits on his eyes, seen through the clear lenses — the lashes, the iris texture and the fine creases at the outer corners are resolved — together with the rim of the acetate frame and the pores across the near cheekbone and the nose. The plane of sharpness carries the whole face, the stubble and the front of the hair. The far ear and the far side of the jaw are marginally soft. The shoulders and the neckband are slightly soft. The backdrop is entirely off the plane of sharpness and reads perfectly smooth.

COLOUR — One saturated family behind, and skin in front of it. The backdrop owns all the magenta and violet in the picture, and that colour is allowed to spill only onto the far side of his face, his far ear and the loose hairs at his crown. The lit side of his face must stay skin-coloured — warm, golden, with red at the nostril, the lips and the near ear — and must not be tinted magenta; the picture fails the moment the whole face reads as one colour. The sweatshirt is neutral black and picks up no cast. The acetate is colourless. The reflections on the lenses are pale blue-white and are the only cool values in the frame. There is no green and no orange anywhere.

CAPTURE — A real exposure made on a full-frame camera in a studio. Light falls off toward the four corners. The reflections on the lenses clip softly and keep their soft edges; the brightest strands at the crown of the hair clip hard and stay very small. Shadows stay open and slightly lifted — the black sweatshirt holds a trace of its nap and its shoulder line rather than collapsing into a void, and the darkest corner of the backdrop sits well above pure black. Skin tone varies across the face rather than running uniform: redder at the ears, the nostrils and the lower lip, paler and cooler across the forehead, with visible fine lines across the forehead and beside the eyes, folds beside the nose, a slight sheen on the forehead and the point of the nose, and small individual blemishes and enlarged pores across the cheeks and nose. Pores, individual stubble hairs, single hairs in the brows and free strands at the crown are all resolved. Visible fine grain throughout, heavier in the dark sweatshirt and in the deepest corners of the backdrop.

FINAL CHECK — One adult man, alone, head level and turned slightly to camera left, his eyes looking off past the lens to the upper right — not into it. His head is a little under half the frame height with about a tenth of the frame height of backdrop above it; the black sweatshirt fills the lower third. The glasses are transparent, not tinted, and the eyes are fully visible through them. The backdrop is a smooth magenta-to-violet gradient, and the lit side of his face stays skin-coloured rather than turning magenta. Do not turn his eyes to the lens and do not widen the shot.

title: Casal sorridente e elegante em camisas brancas
description: Dois homens sorridentes em camisas brancas, com um deles abraçando o outro, transmitindo afeto e conexão em um fundo neutro.
prompt:
SWAP SLOT — TWO IDENTITIES, TWO IMAGES. This picture contains two men, and each one has his own reference. Image 1 is the identity of the man on the LEFT of the frame. Image 2 is the identity of the man on the RIGHT of the frame. From each image take only that man's face, skin tone, hair colour and texture, facial hair, and head and body proportions, and apply them only to his own side of the picture. Do not carry any feature from image 1 onto the man on the right, and do not carry any feature from image 2 onto the man on the left: they are two different people and must remain visibly different in face shape, hair and age. Take nothing else from either image — not the clothing, not the pose, not the expression, not the framing, not the lighting, not the background, not the colour palette. Everything else is built from the text below.

THE PICTURE — A vertical studio portrait of two adult men, together in one frame, standing pressed close side by side in matching white shirts against a plain light grey background, their heads leaning in until they touch, both smiling and looking straight into the lens, with the man on the right holding the other man's arm.

THE READING — This is a portrait about closeness between two people, and it is produced by physical contact, not by expression alone. Their heads are actually touching — the side of one head resting against the side of the other — and that single point of contact is what the whole picture is about; two people merely standing near each other would not read the same. One man's hand grips the other's arm, so the connection is held rather than passive. They are dressed identically in plain white, which removes any difference of role or status between them and makes them a pair. The background is empty and the light is even and open, so there is no drama and no context — nothing to look at except the two faces and the fact that they are joined. Both are smiling with their eyes, not just their mouths, and both are looking directly at the viewer, so the picture is offered rather than observed.

FRAMING AND CAMERA — Aspect ratio 4:5, vertical. Two subjects, half length, side by side and filling the frame. The top edge passes just above the highest point of both heads, leaving a gap of about one fiftieth of the frame height. Each head, from the top of the hair or scalp to the point of the chin, measures about one third of the frame height. The left man's head is centred at about three tenths of the frame width and the right man's at about seven tenths, and the two heads together occupy the central three fifths of the frame with their inner edges touching. The bottom edge of the frame crosses both torsos at about waist level, and both bodies continue past it. The left edge crosses the left man's shoulder and upper arm, and the right edge crosses the right man's shoulder and upper arm; both men's arms continue past those edges. Lens 105mm, camera at their eye level, held perfectly level with no tilt, positioned square to them. Aperture f/5.6, chosen so that both faces sit on the same plane of sharpness.

POSE — Both men stand upright, facing the camera nearly frontally, their bodies overlapping so that the right man stands a little behind and to the right of the left man, his near shoulder passing behind the other's far shoulder. Both men's shoulders are relaxed and dropped. They lean their heads toward one another until they meet: the left man tilts his head about fifteen degrees toward the right of the frame, and the right man tilts his about ten degrees toward the left, so that the right side of the left man's head rests against the left side of the right man's head, temple to temple and cheek to cheek, the skin and hair pressing lightly together at that contact and flattening slightly where they meet. Despite the contact, both faces remain complete and fully separate — two distinct heads with two distinct outlines, not one shape. Both men look straight into the lens, their eyes level. The right man reaches his near arm across the front of the other man in an unbroken line from shoulder to upper arm to elbow to forearm to wrist to hand: the forearm lies diagonally across the lower left of the frame with its white shirt cuff clearly visible, and the hand comes to rest on the left man's far upper arm, the four fingers spread open and slightly curved, lying flat across the sleeve with the fingertips pressing just enough to dimple the cloth, the thumb tucked round behind the arm. The left man's own arms hang down at his sides and continue past the bottom edge.

EXPRESSION — Both men wear the same expression and it is a genuine smile in both cases. The cheeks lift high, pushing the lower eyelids up so each eye narrows into a shallow curve and fine creases fan outward from the outer corners. The corners of the mouth are pulled up and back, deepening the fold that runs from each nostril to the corner of the mouth, and the lips part just enough to show the upper teeth with the lower lip relaxed. The brows sit level and untensed, with only faint settled horizontal lines across the forehead. The nostrils widen a fraction. In both faces the whole upper face moves with the mouth rather than staying still, and the jaw is loose and unclenched.

HAIR — The left man: the head from image 1, worn shaved bare and smooth over the whole scalp with no stubble line, so the light travels across it in one continuous graduated pass and the shape of the skull is fully readable, and the skin of the scalp carries its own small moles, freckles and slight surface irregularities scattered unevenly rather than distributed regularly. Clean-shaven face with no beard, only a faint shadow of hair beneath the skin along the jaw. The right man: the hair from image 2, worn long enough to reach below the ears, wavy and swept back from the forehead and behind the ears with volume at the sides, several loose strands lifting free at the crown and resolving individually at the outline against the background. A full short beard and moustache follow his jaw and upper lip, denser at the chin and thinning up the cheek, with grey hairs mixed unevenly through the darker ones rather than grouped in patches, and the individual hairs visible where the light grazes across them.

WARDROBE — Both men wear the same garment: a plain white cotton poplin shirt, crisply pressed, with a spread collar and a front placket of small round mother-of-pearl buttons. The poplin is smooth with a faint lustre, so it returns a soft even glow across the broad areas and a gentle sheen along the crest of each fold rather than a hard highlight, and the fine weave of the cotton is visible where the light rakes across the shoulder. Each collar stands crisp and open at the throat: the left man's shirt is unbuttoned at the top button only, his collar points sitting close together; the right man's is unbuttoned two buttons, his collar points falling further apart and a small area of chest showing between them. The shirts break into soft rounded folds at the inside of the bent elbow and across the placket, and each button catches one small soft highlight on its domed face. The white of the shirts is the brightest surface in the frame, about a stop and a half above the lit skin. No pattern, no logo, no other garment, no jewellery.

LIGHTING — A single very large soft source placed high and close, slightly to camera left and well forward of both men, angled down about twenty-five degrees. The light is broad enough that it wraps both faces almost equally, so the modelling is gentle: the brow drops a soft wide band onto the upper lids, the nose lays a short soft shadow down and slightly to the right onto the upper lip, the lower lip drops a small shadow onto the chin, and each chin drops a soft shadow onto the throat and the collar. The shadow side of each face sits only about one stop below the lit side and stays completely open. Where the two heads meet, a narrow soft shadow gathers in the crevice between them, dark enough to keep the two heads separate but never hard-edged. The reaching hand and forearm sit about half a stop below the faces. The background is about half a stop below the lit skin, brightest in a broad pool behind and above their heads and falling off gently toward all four corners, the two bottom corners darkest, with a soft shadow of both figures gathering close behind their shoulders. Every transition curves with the surface it crosses; nothing is straight-edged. The lighting sets brightness and falloff only.

BACKGROUND — A plain smooth studio wall or seamless backdrop in a light neutral grey, unbroken, with no seam, texture, object, edge or line anywhere on it. Its surface is matte and paper-like with a very fine even tooth. Depth comes from two things only: the luminance gradient across it, and the soft shadow gathering close behind the two men.

FOCUS — Depth-of-field blur only, no motion blur anywhere; every edge in the picture is a still edge. Both faces are equally and critically sharp — neither man is softer than the other. On both, the lashes, the iris texture, the pores across the cheeks and nose and the fine creases at the outer corners of the eyes are fully resolved, as are the moles on the left man's scalp and the individual beard hairs on the right man's jaw. The plane of sharpness carries both collars and the front of both shirts. The reaching hand, being nearer the lens, is very slightly softer, with the skin texture just beginning to smooth. The outer shoulders are slightly soft. The background is entirely off the plane of sharpness and reads smooth.

COLOUR — A near-monochrome picture with skin as its only real colour. The background is a true neutral grey with no tint of any kind — not blue-grey, not warm-grey. The shirts are neutral white and pick up no cast from anything around them. Against those two neutrals, both men's skin holds its own warmth: golden and slightly ruddy, with red concentrated at the ears, the nostrils, the lips and the fingertips, and both men are warm in the same way so neither reads cooler than the other. Hair and beard are natural brown with grey mixed in. There is no other hue anywhere in the frame.

CAPTURE — A real exposure made on a full-frame camera in a studio. Light falls off gently toward the four corners. The brightest folds of the white shirts clip softly and keep their shape — the shirts must not blow out into flat featureless white — and the small highlights on the buttons and on the crown of the bald scalp clip hard and stay very small. Shadows stay open everywhere; the deepest value in the frame, in the crevice between the two heads, sits well above pure black. Skin tone varies across each face rather than running uniform: redder at the ears, nostrils and lower lip, cooler across the forehead, with a light sheen on the forehead, the nose and the point of each cheekbone. Both faces carry their own real skin: pores, fine lines at the eyes and forehead, folds beside the nose, small moles and blemishes of differing sizes scattered unevenly, and on the left man a visible freckling across the scalp and cheeks. Individual eyebrow hairs, single beard hairs and loose strands at the right man's hairline are all resolved. Very slight fine grain throughout, a little heavier in the corners of the background.

FINAL CHECK — Two men, two separate and complete faces, both fully inside the frame and both critically sharp. The man on the left has the identity of image 1 and the man on the right the identity of image 2, and no feature from either has crossed to the other. Their heads lean in and touch, temple to temple, with a soft dark crevice separating the two outlines so the heads never merge into one shape; both are smiling with the eyes creasing and both look straight into the lens; the right man's hand rests on the other's far upper arm with the fingers spread. Do not blend the two faces and do not drop either man from the picture.

title: Fragrância Masculina Veridium: Frescor Cítrico na Água
description: Um perfume masculino com notas cítricas, exibido em um leito de água ondulante com fatias de toranja e limão, e folhas verdes com gotas de orvalho.
prompt:
SWAP SLOT 1 — THE PRODUCT. Image 1 is the product reference. Take from it only the physical object: the shape and proportions of the bottle, the material and colour of the glass, the shape, finish and colour of the cap, the colour of the liquid inside, and the design, layout and wording of the label exactly as printed on it. Take nothing else from image 1 — not its background, not its surface, not its lighting, not its shadows, not its colour palette, not its mood, not any prop appearing beside it, and not the angle it was shot from. The product is placed into the scene described below and lit by the lights described below. If image 1 is a cut-out on white, a shot on a dark reflective plinth, or a lifestyle photograph, none of that carries over.

SWAP SLOT 2 — THE BOTANICALS. As written, this scene uses citrus and glossy green leaves: two halved grapefruits with the cut face up, two whole citrus slices, and three or four dark waxy leaves. To match a different product, substitute different botanicals, but keep the arrangement and the material logic identical: two large cut faces showing internal structure, two smaller flat pieces, and three or four leaves or petals. Whatever is substituted must be described the same way — by what its surface does to light, not by its name. A cut face gets its internal structure and its translucency; a flat piece gets its edge and its thickness; a leaf or petal gets its cuticle and its vein pattern and how water sits on it. Never name a botanical without describing its optical behaviour, or it will come back looking like plastic.

THE PICTURE — A vertical product photograph of a single perfume bottle standing in a shallow pool of dark blue-green water, seen from high above and slightly in front, with cut citrus and wet green leaves floating on the water around it and ripples spreading out from the bottle across the surface.

THE READING — This is a commercial product photograph, and everything in it exists to make one object look expensive and cold-fresh. The product is dead centre and upright, the only vertical thing in a frame of flat horizontal surface, so it reads as standing while everything else lies down. The botanicals are arranged around it in a loose ring but never touch it and never overlap its label, so the eye is led inward and then held. The water is dark and the product is bright, so the bottle is the only thing the eye can settle on. And the freshness is carried entirely by physical evidence — beaded droplets, ripples, bubbles caught under the surface, cut fruit still wet — not by brightness or by colour saturation.

FRAMING AND CAMERA — Aspect ratio 4:5, vertical. The camera is high above the water and angled steeply downward, about seventy degrees from horizontal, so the water surface fills the entire frame from edge to edge and recedes only slightly; there is no horizon, no wall and no edge of the pool anywhere in the picture. The bottle stands upright in the shallow water and is seen from above and in front, so its front label faces the lens squarely and fully readable while the top of its cap is also visible. The bottle is centred horizontally, its centre at about half the frame width. Including the cap, it spans about three fifths of the frame height, its cap top about one fifth of the frame height below the top edge and its base about one fifth of the frame height above the bottom edge. The bottle's body is about half the frame width. The botanicals sit in a loose ring around it: a large halved fruit at the upper left, crossed by the left edge so part of it continues past the frame; a round slice below it on the left; a second round slice at the middle right; a second halved fruit at the lower right, crossed by the right edge and continuing past it; and leaves at the top centre, the upper left corner, the middle left edge and the bottom centre right, the last one crossed by the bottom edge and continuing past it. Nothing overlaps the label. Lens 100mm macro, aperture f/8.

THE HERO EFFECT — The water. It is the surface everything rests on and the reason the picture works, and it must be built from four separate behaviours, all present at once.

First, the ripples. A set of concentric rings spreads outward from the base of the bottle, tightest and sharpest close to it and progressively wider and lower in amplitude as they travel out, dying away before they reach the frame edges. The rings are not perfect circles and not evenly spaced: they wobble, they are interrupted where they pass a floating object, and a second weaker set radiates from the lower right where another disturbance began, crossing the first set and producing an interference pattern of small raised and flattened patches where the two meet. Each ripple crest catches light along its leading edge and drops dark along its trailing side, so the whole surface reads as a field of fine curved bright and dark bands rather than as a flat plane.

Second, the caustics. The light passing through the moving surface is focused and scattered onto the shallow bottom beneath, producing a net of bright wandering lines that pool and cross and brighten where they overlap, strongest in the upper right where the light is strongest and fading toward the lower left. These caustic lines lie beneath the surface and are visibly separated from the ripples above them, softer and more diffuse than the surface highlights.

Third, the waterline on every object. Each floating item sits partly in and partly out: the water climbs slightly up the side of each piece of fruit into a thin curved meniscus that catches a fine bright line, the submerged part of each object is dimmer, greener and slightly displaced sideways by refraction, and small clusters of air bubbles cling under the edges of the rinds and along the leaf margins, each bubble a tiny sphere with a bright ring and a dark centre, varying in size and clustering irregularly rather than sitting in an even row. Around the base of the bottle the water is shallow enough that the glass foot and the surface meet in a bright irregular ring.

Fourth, the droplets on the dry surfaces. On the bottle's glass and on the cap, water sits as separate raised beads rather than as a sheet, because the surface repels it: each bead is a small lens with a bright rim, a darker centre where it inverts what is behind it, and one small hard white specular on its upper side, and the beads vary in size, cluster unevenly, overlap into occasional larger doubled beads, and sit at slightly different degrees of focus depending on where they are on the curved surface. On the leaves the beading is even more pronounced — high domed drops standing almost spherical on the waxy cuticle.

PROPS AND OBJECTS — Two halved grapefruits, cut face turned up toward the lens: the flesh is a translucent coral-pink, organised into radial segments separated by thin pale membranes, each segment packed with fine juice vesicles that scatter light and glow slightly where light passes through them from the side, brightest at the segment edges and deeper in colour toward the centre. A ring of soft white pith surrounds the flesh, matte and opaque and completely without shine, and outside it a thin rind in warm orange whose surface is pitted with small oil glands, each pit reading as a tiny shadowed dimple. The cut faces are wet, so a thin film of juice lies across them and returns a broad soft sheen, and a few loose droplets sit on the surface. Two whole citrus slices in yellow-green, cut thin enough to be translucent: light passes through the flesh so each segment glows from behind, the white central core reads as an opaque star, and the rind edge is a clean bright ring with its own visible oil pitting. Three or four dark green leaves, oval with a pointed tip: their upper surface is a waxy cuticle that lays one broad soft sheen along the length of the leaf and shows a raised pale midrib with lateral veins branching from it in an irregular, unequal pattern; the wax repels water, so drops stand on them as raised domes rather than spreading, and each leaf is bent slightly along its own axis rather than lying flat.

THE PRODUCT AS IT SITS IN THE SCENE — Whatever the bottle's form, its materials behave as follows in this light. Clear glass: thick, so its vertical corners concentrate light into bright narrow bands and its base acts as a lens, magnifying and displacing the water and the fruit seen through it, and everything visible through the glass is refracted — shifted sideways, inverted or compressed relative to what lies beside it, never simply seen through as if the glass were a window. The liquid inside is nearly clear, so the bottle reads mostly as glass and air with a shift in tone where the liquid level sits. A polished metal cap: a true mirror, returning a compressed distorted reflection of everything around it — the orange of the nearest fruit appears on it as a smeared coloured patch, the dark water as a broad dark band, and one bright vertical highlight runs down the side facing the light. At the single brightest point on the cap, the specular is intense enough to bloom into a small four-pointed star. The label is a flat matte paper face that takes light evenly and returns no reflection at all, so it reads a full stop flatter than everything around it, and it is the one perfectly still, perfectly clean rectangle in a picture otherwise full of texture — nothing floats in front of it and no droplet sits on it.

LIGHTING — A single hard source placed high and behind the scene, to the upper right, angled down across the water toward the camera. Because it is hard and raking, it puts a crisp bright edge on every ripple crest in the upper right and lets the lower left of the surface fall about two stops darker. It drives the caustics on the bottom. It puts one bright vertical highlight down the side of the cap and the four-pointed star at its brightest point. It rims the wet edge of each piece of fruit and each leaf with a fine bright line where the meniscus curves. It passes through the thin citrus slices from behind so their flesh glows from within, and it strikes the cut faces of the halved fruit at a glancing angle so the wet film on them returns a broad sheen. A second, much weaker soft fill comes from the front and slightly above, opening the shadow side of the bottle and lifting the label so it stays evenly lit. The label is the brightest matte surface in the frame; the specular on the cap is the brightest point of all. The water in the lower left corner is the darkest area. Every transition curves with the surface it crosses; nothing is straight-edged. The lighting sets brightness and falloff only.

BACKGROUND — There is no background other than the water itself and what lies just beneath it: a shallow dark bottom in deep blue-green, its detail dissolved and readable only through the caustic net playing across it. No horizon, no wall, no vessel edge, no visible container, no floor. Depth is carried by three separations: the objects floating on the surface, the surface itself with its ripples, and the caustic-lit bottom beneath.

FOCUS — Depth-of-field blur only, no motion blur anywhere; every edge is a still edge and the ripples are frozen rather than smeared. Critical sharpness sits on the label and the front face of the bottle — the printed edges, the paper grain and every droplet on the glass are resolved. The plane of sharpness carries the cap and the nearest ripples. The fruit at the middle left and middle right is very slightly softer, with the juice vesicles still individually resolved. The halved fruit at the upper left and lower right, being furthest from the plane, is a step softer again. The caustics on the bottom are soft. The outermost corners of the water are the softest areas in the frame.

COLOUR — Two families in strict opposition. Cool: the water is a deep desaturated blue-green, the shadowed troughs of the ripples nearly navy, and it must stay green-blue rather than drifting to pure blue or to grey. Warm: the coral-pink flesh and orange rind of the halved fruit, the yellow of the slices, and the gold of the cap. The leaves are a saturated mid-green that sits between the two families and belongs to neither. The label is neutral white with its printed marks in a dark navy, and it is the only pure neutral in the frame. There is no purple, no red-orange bleeding into the water, and no warm cast anywhere on the water's surface.

CAPTURE — A real exposure made on a medium-format camera with studio strobe. Light falls off toward the four corners, the lower left darkest. The specular on the cap clips hard and blooms into its star; the brightest ripple crests and the specular points on the droplets clip hard and stay very small; the wet sheen on the cut fruit clips softly and keeps its shape. Shadows stay open — the dark water holds readable ripple structure rather than collapsing into flat black. Colour varies within each object rather than running uniform: the grapefruit flesh is deeper at its centre and paler at its edges, the rind varies along its length, the leaves are lighter along the midrib. Every repeated element in the picture varies — no two droplets are the same size, no two bubbles are evenly spaced, no two ripples are the same width. Very slight fine grain throughout, heavier in the dark water.

FINAL CHECK — One bottle, alone, standing upright and centred, spanning about three fifths of the frame height, its label facing the lens and completely unobscured. The camera is high and angled steeply down onto water that fills the frame edge to edge with no horizon and no visible container. Concentric ripples spread from the bottle's base, caustics play on the bottom, water beads on the glass and the cap as separate raised drops, and the botanicals float around the bottle without touching it or covering the label. Do not lower the camera to a side view and do not let anything overlap the label.

title: Retrato Dramático de Robert Downey Jr.
description: Um retrato dramático de Robert Downey Jr. com iluminação de estúdio vibrante, capturando sua expressão pensativa e intensa.
prompt:
SWAP SLOT — Image 1 is the identity reference. Take from it only the face, the skin tone, the hair colour and texture, and the head and body proportions of the person in this picture. Take nothing else from it: not the clothing, not the pose, not the expression, not the framing, not the lighting, not the background, not the colour palette, not the mood. Everything else in this picture is built from the text below. If image 1 shows different clothes or a different setting, ignore them completely.

THE PICTURE — A vertical bust portrait of one adult man, alone, in a dark suit, white shirt and dark tie, photographed from below with his chin raised and his eyes looking up and past the camera, lit by two coloured sources of opposite temperature that meet across his face, against a flat saturated orange backdrop.

THE READING — This is a portrait of resolve, and it is produced by physical facts rather than by mood. The camera sits below his chin and tilts up, so the viewer looks up at him and the underside of his jaw, the line of his throat and the base of his nose are all in view — the angle of a monument. His chin is raised and his neck is extended, which exposes the throat; combined with the low camera that reads as conviction rather than as vulnerability. His eyes are aimed up and past the lens at something outside the frame, so he is not addressing the viewer at all — he is looking at whatever he has decided about. His head is large in the frame and pressed close to the top edge, so the frame is barely able to hold it. His mouth is closed and completely still, and nothing in the face is straining; the whole picture rests on the angle, the gaze and the two colours crossing him.

FRAMING AND CAMERA — Aspect ratio 4:5, vertical. Single subject, bust length. The top edge of the frame passes just above the crown of his hair, leaving a gap of about one twentieth of the frame height, so the head is pressed hard against the top of the picture. His head, from the top of the hair to the point of the chin, measures about half the frame height. It is centred just left of the middle of the frame, its centre at about forty-seven hundredths of the frame width. The bottom edge of the frame crosses his chest at about the middle of the tie blade, and his torso continues past it. His shoulders run almost the full width of the frame, and the left and right edges each cross the top of a shoulder, both continuing past those edges. Lens 85mm, camera positioned well below his chin — roughly at the level of his sternum — and tilted upward about eighteen degrees, so the underside of the jaw, the base of the nose and the front of the throat are all visible and the head reads as being seen from beneath. Aperture f/4.

POSE — He stands upright, shoulders square to the lens and level, held down and relaxed, with only a few degrees of rotation toward camera right. His neck is extended and his head is tilted back so the chin rises about twenty degrees above level, and the head is turned about ten degrees toward camera right so the face is very slightly off-frontal. His eyes are aimed up and to the right of the lens at a point above and beyond the frame, the irises sitting high in the eye openings with a band of white visible beneath each one. Both arms hang down at his sides in an unbroken line from shoulder to upper arm, and both continue past the left and right edges of the frame. The shoulders carry no lift and the throat is not tensed.

EXPRESSION — The brows sit level and lifted very slightly, drawing three faint horizontal creases across the forehead, with no furrow between them. The upper eyelids are open and steady and the lower lids are relaxed, the eyes held on their distant point without narrowing. The nostrils are relaxed. The lips are closed and lightly together, the corners level with a faint downward set, the lower lip full and unpressed. The jaw is loose rather than clenched. The cheeks are still. Nothing in the face is performing; the expression is entirely settled.

HAIR — The hair from image 1, worn medium length and swept up and back off the forehead into a raised, textured shape, the strands clearly separated rather than lying as a smooth mass, with several standing free at the crown and along the front edge where the light rims them, and shorter and closer at the sides and above the ears. Because two sources of different colour reach it, the strands on one side of the head are rimmed cool and those on the other are rimmed warm, with individual filaments picking up one colour or the other along their length. A short beard and moustache follow the jaw and the upper lip at a close trimmed length, denser at the chin and thinning up the cheek, with individual hairs and the skin between them both visible and a scattering of grey hairs mixed unevenly through the darker ones rather than grouped.

WARDROBE — A dark suit jacket in a matte worsted wool: the fabric absorbs almost all the light and reads as the deepest, flattest tone in the frame, showing shape only as a faint lift along the crest of each shoulder and along the folded edge of the lapel. It takes the colour of whatever light reaches it, so one shoulder sits a deep cool blue-black and the other a deep dark red-black. The lapel is a notch lapel with a crisp pressed edge that catches a thin line of light along its length. Under it a white cotton poplin shirt, crisply pressed with a pointed collar standing clean on both sides of the neck: the poplin is smooth and slightly lustrous, and because it is the only genuinely white surface on him it shows each source's colour more purely than anything else — cool on one side, warm on the other — with a soft sheen along each fold rather than a hard highlight. A dark tie in a matte silk, knotted small and tight at the throat, its blade running straight down the centre of the chest, reading nearly as dark as the suit but flatter and smoother, with one narrow soft highlight along the roll of the knot and another along the blade's near edge. No pattern anywhere.

THE HERO EFFECT — Two colours crossing one face. Two hard sources reach him from opposite sides. One is cool — a pale cyan-teal — placed forward and to camera left, a little above his eye level. The other is warm — a saturated red — placed to camera right, slightly behind him and above, so it rakes across that side of the head rather than facing it. Each light dies where the surface it is travelling across turns away from it, and that is what creates the meeting, so the boundary between the two is never a line and never straight. Written as consequence: the cool light runs across the forehead, down the near side of the nose and across the near cheekbone, and stops at the ridge of the nose because the far slope of the nose is turned away from it; it drops into the near eye socket and leaves the deepest part of it unlit; it lays a short shadow of the nose down onto the upper lip; and it fades out along the near side of the jaw. The warm light picks up exactly where the cool one fails: it catches the far slope of the nose and the far nostril wing, floods the far cheek, rims the far eyebrow and the far ear, runs down the far side of the neck and pools under the jaw. Because the neck is a cylinder rather than a plane, the two lights meet there in a broad soft blend three or four fingers wide rather than at a seam. Because the cheekbone is a rounded ridge, the transition rides up and over it. Because the eye socket is a hollow, the transition dips into it. Because the chin is a ball, the transition curves around it. Nowhere in the picture does the boundary run straight, and neither colour is applied as an even wash over a flat half of the face. Each source leaves its own catchlight, one cool and one warm, both sitting low in the eyes because he is looking upward.

LIGHTING — The cool source sits about one stop above the warm one on the face, so the cool side reads as the key and the warm side as the accent. Shadow edges from both are crisp with only a narrow gradation. The deepest values on the face are the near eye socket and the far side of the nose bridge, and both stay open and readable rather than blocking to black. The shirt collar is the brightest surface in the frame, about a stop and a half above the lit skin. The suit takes only glancing light and sits three stops below the face. The backdrop is lit separately and evenly by its own source and sits about half a stop below the lit side of his face, brightest in a broad area behind and above his head and falling off toward the four corners, the two bottom corners darkest. Every transition curves with the surface it crosses; nothing is straight-edged. The lighting sets brightness and falloff only.

BACKGROUND — A plain seamless studio backdrop in a strong saturated orange, unbroken, with no seam, texture, object, edge or shadow anywhere on it. Its surface is matte and paper-like with a very fine even tooth. Depth comes from one thing only: the gradual luminance gradient across it, brighter behind the head and sinking toward the corners.

FOCUS — Depth-of-field blur only, no motion blur anywhere; every edge in the picture is a still edge. Critical sharpness sits on his eyes — the lashes, the iris texture and the fine creases at the outer corners are resolved — and across the near cheekbone and the bridge of the nose, where the pores are fully rendered. The plane of sharpness carries the whole face, the beard and the front of the hair. The shirt collar and the tie knot are marginally soft. The shoulders are slightly soft. The backdrop is entirely off the plane of sharpness and reads smooth.

COLOUR — Three families, kept separate and all saturated. The backdrop is a strong orange and owns the entire area around him; nothing of the cyan or the red spills onto it. On him, one side is cool cyan-teal and the other is red, and the two must not average into a single warm or single cool face — the picture fails the moment both sides read the same temperature. The suit is a near-black that takes those two colours rather than a colour of its own. The shirt is white and shows each source at its purest. His skin holds its own tone underneath both lights: it is skin coloured by cyan and skin coloured by red, still reading as flesh with texture and blood in it, not as painted surfaces. There is no green and no neutral grey anywhere in the frame.

CAPTURE — A real exposure made on a full-frame camera in a studio. Light falls off toward the four corners. The brightest points on the shirt collar and the highest strands of hair clip hard to white and stay small; the red on the far cheekbone and the tip of the nose clips softly and keeps its modelling. Shadows stay open — the suit holds a trace of its weave and its shoulder line rather than collapsing into a void, and the deepest value on the face sits well above pure black. Skin tone varies rather than running uniform: redder at the ears, the nostrils and the lips, and visibly different in texture across the face, with deep settled lines across the forehead, crow's feet at the outer corners of the eyes, folds beside the nose, a slight sheen on the forehead and the point of the nose, and small individual blemishes and enlarged pores across the cheeks and nose. Pores, individual beard hairs, single grey hairs and free strands at the crown are all resolved. Visible fine grain throughout, heavier in the dark suit and in the corners of the backdrop.

FINAL CHECK — One adult man, alone. Camera below his chin and tilted up, so the underside of the jaw and the base of the nose are visible; his head about half the frame height and pressed close to the top edge; his chin raised and his eyes looking up and past the lens, not into it. One side of the face is lit cool cyan and the other red, and the boundary between them curves with the anatomy it crosses — it is never a straight line and never a flat half. The backdrop is plain saturated orange. Do not lower the camera and do not turn his eyes to the lens.

title: Brad Pitt com Óculos e Sorriso Acolhedor
description: Um retrato de Brad Pitt usando óculos, sorrindo gentilmente sob uma iluminação suave e quente, transmitindo uma aura sofisticada e acolhedora.
prompt:
SWAP SLOT — Image 1 is the identity reference. Take from it only the face, the skin tone, the hair colour and texture, and the head and body proportions of the person in this picture. Take nothing else from it: not the clothing, not the eyewear, not the pose, not the expression, not the framing, not the lighting, not the background, not the colour palette, not the mood. Everything else in this picture is built from the text below. If image 1 shows different clothes or a different setting, ignore them completely.

THE PICTURE — A vertical bust portrait of one adult man, alone, facing the camera dead-on in a plain black crew-neck t-shirt and thin round gold glasses, smiling with his mouth closed, standing in front of a dark textured wall onto which a large warm amber disc of light is projected behind his head.

THE READING — This portrait is about warmth and openness, and it is produced by physical facts rather than by mood. The smile is genuine and the proof is anatomical: the cheeks lift and push the lower eyelids up, so the eyes narrow into shallow curves and crease at the outer corners — the upper face moves with the mouth instead of staying still, which is the entire difference between a warm portrait and a posed one. He wears a plain black t-shirt with no collar, no tailoring and no status object, so nothing in the wardrobe is asking to be read. His head is large in the frame and close to the lens, and the light on his face is soft and comes from the front, so the proximity reads as intimacy rather than as confrontation. The disc behind him is warm and low in intensity, sitting just behind his head like a halo, and it must not be brighter than his face — the moment it dominates, the picture becomes theatrical instead of friendly. And the composition is symmetrical and frontal, with nothing tilted or turned, so the picture is direct and easy to look at.

FRAMING AND CAMERA — Aspect ratio 4:5, vertical. Single subject, bust length, centred: his head is centred at half the frame width and the composition is symmetrical about that centre line. The top edge of the frame sits about one tenth of the frame height above the crown of his hair. His head, from the top of the hair to the point of the chin, measures just under half the frame height, so it is large and close. The bottom edge of the frame crosses his chest a little below the collarbone, and his torso continues past it. The left and right edges each cross the top of a shoulder, and both shoulders continue past those edges. The projected disc behind him is a circle whose diameter measures about four fifths of the frame width, its centre a little above the centre of his head, its topmost arc about one eleventh of the frame height below the top edge, and its lower portion occluded by his head and shoulders so only its left and right arcs come down past his ears. Lens 85mm, camera at his eye level, held perfectly level with no tilt, positioned square to him so there is no rotation. Aperture f/2.8.

POSE — He stands upright and completely frontal, shoulders square to the lens and level with each other, held down and relaxed, weight even with no hip shift. His torso is not rotated. His head is upright, level, turned dead-on to the camera, the chin carried level rather than tucked or lifted. His eyes are aimed straight into the lens. Both arms hang down at his sides in an unbroken line from shoulder to upper arm, and both continue past the left and right edges of the frame. The neck is loose and the shoulders carry no lift.

EXPRESSION — The cheeks lift high, pushing the lower eyelids up so each eye narrows into a shallow curve and fine creases fan outward from the outer corners. The corners of the mouth are pulled up and back and the lips stay together, so no teeth show; the fold running from each nostril to the corner of the mouth deepens and a small dimple forms in the near cheek. The brows sit level and untensed with no crease between them, and two faint settled horizontal lines cross the forehead. The nostrils widen a fraction. The whole upper face moves with the mouth rather than staying still, and the jaw is loose and unclenched.

HAIR — The hair from image 1, worn short and tight at the sides and back and left longer on top, swept up and back off the forehead into a raised textured shape with the individual strands clearly separated rather than lying as a smooth mass, several standing free at the crown and along the front edge where the light catches them as bright single filaments. A light irregular stubble across the jaw, the chin and the upper lip, sparse enough that individual hairs and the skin between them are both visible, denser at the chin and thinning up the cheek.

WARDROBE — A plain black cotton jersey t-shirt with a ribbed crew neckline. The jersey is matte and slightly fuzzy, absorbing almost all the light, so it reads as the deepest, flattest black in the frame and shows form only as a faint lift toward warm grey along the crest of each shoulder and along the top of the neckline's ribbing. The ribbed band at the neck is the one place the fabric has structure: each raised rib takes a thin warm line of light on its crest and goes dark in the channel between. The shirt is otherwise unbroken — no collar, no print, no pattern, no logo, no seam visible across the chest. A very thin gold chain lies against the skin at the base of his throat, so fine it reads as a broken line of tiny hard pinpoints rather than as a continuous object.

PROPS AND OBJECTS — Round glasses with thin pale gold wire frames: a slim straight bridge, small round rims, and fine temple arms running back over the ear. The lenses are clear and untinted — his eyes, lashes and the lower parts of his brows are fully visible through them, undistorted and only very slightly darkened. The wire rim traces one thin unbroken bright line along the upper curve of each lens where it faces the light, and each lens carries one soft, low-contrast reflection across its upper outer corner, faint enough that it never obscures the eye behind it.

THE HERO EFFECT — The projected disc. Behind him, on the wall, is a circle of warm amber light thrown by a single hard source aimed past him. It is a filled disc, not a ring: the light covers the whole circle, brightest a little above and left of its centre and falling off gently toward its own edge. Its outer boundary is defined but not razor-cut — the light drops from full to nothing across a soft band roughly one twentieth of the disc's diameter wide, and that band is even all the way round. Outside it the wall goes dark and cool. The disc is light landing on a surface, not a surface that glows, and three things prove it: the wall's own texture stays fully visible inside the lit area, brighter on the crest of every grain and shadowed in every pit; the disc's tone shifts slightly across its own face rather than being flat; and his own shadow falls onto it. That shadow is the most important part — a soft-edged dark shape of his head and near shoulder, cast down and to the right, its edge widening as it travels away from him, its interior a warm dark brown rather than a neutral grey because it is a shadow inside coloured light. Without that cast shadow the disc reads as a glowing object behind him instead of light on a wall.

LIGHTING — A single hard source placed forward and to camera left, above his eye level, aimed slightly past him at the wall, and softened just enough that its shadows have narrow gradual edges rather than hard ones. On his face it lays a broad warm pass across the forehead, the near cheekbone, the nose and the near side of the jaw, with the far side of the face about a stop and a half down and fully open. The brow drops a soft band onto the upper lids, the nose lays a short soft shadow down and to the right onto the cheek, the lower lip drops a small shadow onto the chin, and the chin drops a soft shadow onto the throat. The top of his hair, being nearest the source, is the brightest area on him and clips softly at the crown. The black t-shirt takes almost nothing and sits four stops below the face. The disc on the wall sits about half a stop below the lit side of his face — it is warm and present but never brighter than he is — and the wall outside the disc sits about three and a half stops below it. Every transition curves with the surface it crosses; nothing is straight-edged. The lighting sets brightness and falloff only.

BACKGROUND — A flat wall of rendered plaster with a fine granular texture: a dense irregular surface of tiny raised grains and shallow pits, with a few faint vertical trowel marks and one or two small imperfections. It is otherwise unbroken — no seam, corner, object or edge anywhere on it. Its texture is clearly legible inside the lit disc and almost invisible in the dark area outside it. Depth is carried by two things only: the disc and its falloff, and his cast shadow lying on the wall.

FOCUS — Depth-of-field blur only, no motion blur anywhere; every edge is a still edge. Critical sharpness sits on his eyes, seen through the clear lenses — individual lashes, the iris texture, the fine creases at the outer corners and the pores across the cheekbone are all resolved — together with the thin gold wire of the frames. The plane of sharpness carries the whole face, the stubble and the front of the hair. The shoulders are very slightly soft. The wall behind is off the plane of sharpness and smooth, its granular texture present but softened, and the edge of the disc is soft from its own falloff rather than from defocus.

COLOUR — Two families, split by the disc's edge. Everything inside the disc and everything on his skin is warm: amber, gold and honey, with the shadows on his face going warm brown rather than grey. Everything outside the disc is cool and dark: the wall reads as a deep cool grey with a faint green-grey cast, and it must not pick up the amber. The t-shirt is neutral black and the chain is warm gold. His skin holds its own warmth on top of the warm light — redder at the ears, the nostrils and the lips, paler across the forehead — rather than being uniformly tinted. There is no blue anywhere and no pure neutral grey inside the disc.

CAPTURE — A real exposure made on a full-frame camera. Light falls off toward the four corners, deepening the two bottom ones most. The brightest strands at the crown of the hair and the pinpoints on the chain clip softly and stay very small; nothing in the frame clips hard to white. Shadows stay open and slightly lifted — the black t-shirt holds a trace of its knit and its shoulder shape rather than collapsing into a void, and the dark wall outside the disc sits well above pure black. Skin tone varies across the face rather than running uniform: redder at the ears, the nostrils and the lower lip, paler and cooler across the forehead, with visible fine lines across the forehead and beside the eyes, small individual blemishes and a slight sheen on the nose and the point of the cheekbone. Pores, individual stubble hairs, single hairs in the brows and free strands at the crown are all resolved. Visible fine grain throughout, heavier in the dark area of the wall, and a gentle soft highlight rolloff rather than an abrupt one.

FINAL CHECK — One adult man, alone, dead-on frontal and symmetrical, his head just under half the frame height and centred, smiling with the mouth closed and the eyes creasing with it. Behind him, a filled amber disc of light about four fifths of the frame width projected onto a textured wall, with his own soft shadow falling across it to the right, and the wall dark and cool outside the circle. Do not turn his head, do not make the disc brighter than his face, and do not remove the cast shadow.

title: Jovem com fone de ouvido e tênis rosa na lavanderia
description: Imagem criativa de um jovem com fones de ouvido segurando um tênis rosa, olhando para dentro de uma máquina de lavar.
prompt:
SWAP SLOT — Image 1 is the identity reference. Take from it only the face, the skin tone, the hair colour and texture, and the head and body proportions of the person in this picture. Take nothing else from it: not the clothing, not the headphones, not the pose, not the expression, not the framing, not the lighting, not the background, not the colour palette, not the mood. Everything else in this picture is built from the text below. If image 1 shows different clothes or a different setting, ignore them completely.

THE PICTURE — A vertical photograph taken from inside the drum of a laundrette washing machine, looking outward through the open porthole: the camera sits down among the wet clothes, and one adult man leans in from the street outside, holding a pink suede trainer out toward the lens and looking straight into it.

THE READING — This is a comic point-of-view picture, and the comedy is produced by position, not by mood. The camera is inside the machine, which puts the viewer in the position of the laundry: he is not looking at a photographer, he is looking into the drum at his own washing. The circular porthole crops him into a hard round aperture and the rest of the frame is dark perforated metal, so the picture has an iris cut into it and everything of interest happens inside that circle. The trainer is pushed forward, close to the lens and larger than it should be, so the shoe reads as the subject and the man as its owner. His mouth is slightly open and his brows are slightly raised, and he is looking dead into the lens — the look of someone finding something in the machine, not the look of someone posing. And the brightness split does the rest: the outside world is open and bright, the inside of the drum is dark and cramped, and the viewer is on the dark side.

FRAMING AND CAMERA — Aspect ratio 4:5, vertical. The camera sits low inside the washing-machine drum, resting among the laundry, pointing straight out through the open door, held level with no tilt.
