The tube itself is thin — about one fortieth of the frame width — and its core is white-hot and fully clipped, while its edges bleed outward into a saturated orange over a very short distance, so the tube reads as a hard white line inside a soft orange one. Around it, the light does not stop at the tube: it pours into the air, and because the space is full of drifting haze, the glow is volumetric. Immediately around the ring the haze is bright orange, and the brightness falls away outward and inward over a long gradient, so the area inside the ring is a warm luminous field and the corners of the frame go deep brown. The haze itself is not uniform: slow curling wisps of smoke drift across the lower left of the ring's interior, varying in density, some thick enough to hide the wall behind them and some barely there, curling and folding rather than lying flat, and the light passing through the denser ones is scattered into visible soft bands. The ring also lights him from behind: it lays a warm orange rim along the top and the side of his hair that varies in width, is brightest where the hair is thin enough to transmit light through it, and breaks completely where the head turns away from it, and a second rim runs down the side of the cheek and along the outer edge of the beard, thinning and interrupting where the beard is dense. It also throws a broad soft orange wash across the top of each shoulder. The rim is uneven everywhere: it must not run as a continuous line of even width around the whole silhouette.

LIGHTING — Two systems. Behind: the ring, described above, which owns everything warm — the rims on the hair, cheek and shoulders, the glow in the haze, and the luminance of the entire background. In front: a single soft neutral source placed close to the camera axis and just above it, which lights the face frontally and flatly, filling both eye sockets, laying a soft shadow under the nose and under the lower lip and a soft band under the jaw, with no strong shadow on either side of the face. The face sits about two stops below the ring's glow in the haze and about four stops below the tube itself. The jacket takes very little of the frontal light and sits about three stops below the face, holding its brightest values on the satin lapel and on the crests of the brocade. Every transition curves with the surface it crosses; nothing is straight-edged. The lighting sets brightness and falloff only.

BACKGROUND — Physically, a dark studio space filled with atmospheric haze, with a plain dark wall far behind the ring. Nothing else is in it: no furniture, no edges, no objects, no visible floor or ceiling. Depth is carried by three separations: the man in front, the ring standing behind him, and the wall and haze receding beyond that.

FOCUS — Depth-of-field blur only, no motion blur anywhere; every edge is a still edge and the smoke is not streaked. Critical sharpness sits on his eyes, seen through the tinted lenses — the lashes, the iris texture and the pores along the cheekbone are resolved — together with the thin wire of the frame, the carved grooves on the shirt buttons and the waffle weave of the shirt. The plane of sharpness carries the whole face, the beard and the front of the jacket. The ring is slightly behind that plane and marginally soft, but its softness comes from bloom rather than from defocus: its edge is spread by the light itself, not smeared. The haze is soft everywhere. The wall behind is dissolved completely.

COLOUR — Two families, hard split. Everything behind him is warm: the ring is white-cored orange, the glow is saturated orange, the haze is amber, and the corners fall to a deep warm brown. Everything on him is cool or neutral: the jacket is a deep navy that must stay blue and never drift to black or to purple, the lapel is neutral black, the shirt is a soft off-white with no colour cast, and the lenses are a cool blue-grey. His skin sits between the two: warm and natural under the frontal light, with red at the ear, the nostril and the lip, and turning distinctly orange only where the ring rims it. There is no green anywhere in the frame, and no neutral grey in the background.

CAPTURE — A real exposure made on a full-frame camera in a hazy studio. Light falls off toward the four corners, deepening the two bottom ones most. The core of the neon tube clips hard to pure white and blooms outward into a soft halation that eats slightly into the outline of his hair where it crosses in front of it; the rims on the hair and cheek clip softly and keep their variation. Shadows stay open — the navy jacket holds its brocade and its colour rather than collapsing to black, and the deepest value in the frame, in the corners, sits above pure black. Skin tone varies across the face rather than running uniform: redder at the ear, the nostril and the lower lip, paler across the forehead, with visible fine lines across the forehead and beside the eyes, a slight sheen on the bridge of the nose and the point of the cheekbone, and small individual blemishes and pores resolved. Individual beard hairs and single combed hair grooves are resolved. Visible fine grain throughout, heavier in the haze and in the dark corners.

FINAL CHECK — One adult man, alone, dead-on frontal and symmetrical, his head about two fifths of the frame height and centred on the frame's vertical axis. A single unbroken glowing ring stands behind his head, concentric with it, its outer diameter about four fifths of the frame width, with its lower arc passing behind his shoulders. The rim light on his hair and cheek is uneven and breaks where the form turns away. Do not turn his head and do not widen the shot.

title: Mulher jovem com telefone vintage vermelho
description: Um retrato de estúdio vibrante e criativo de uma mulher jovem usando um telefone retrô vermelho, capturando sua expressão de surpresa.
prompt:
SWAP SLOT — Image 1 is the identity reference. Take from it only the face, the skin tone, the hair colour and texture, and the head and body proportions of the woman in this picture. Take nothing else from it: not the clothing, not the pose, not the expression, not the framing, not the lighting, not the background, not the colour palette, not the mood. Everything else in this picture is built from the text below. If image 1 shows different clothes or a different setting, ignore them completely.

THE PICTURE — A vertical full-length studio photograph of one adult woman, alone, crouched down on a plain light grey studio floor in an oversized black suit, holding the red handset of a vintage push-button telephone to her ear with one hand while her other hand pulls the coiled cord out sideways, the telephone itself sitting on the floor at the lower left of the frame.

THE READING — This is a picture about energy and comic timing, and both are produced by physical facts rather than by mood. The body is in a deep crouch with the heels lifted — an unstable, athletic position that cannot be held for long, so the pose reads as caught mid-moment rather than posed. The cord is pulled taut into a nearly straight horizontal line across the frame, and that single line of tension is what carries the movement: the picture would go flat if the cord hung slack. The suit is several sizes too large, the shoulders extending well beyond her own and the sleeves reaching the knuckles, so the tailoring plays against the small folded body inside it. The props sit on the floor rather than on a desk, which places everything at ground level and makes the crouch necessary rather than decorative. Her mouth is open in a full smile and her brows are raised, and her eyes are aimed straight into the lens, so the viewer is the person she is reacting to. Nothing about the picture is still.

FRAMING AND CAMERA — Aspect ratio 4:5, vertical. Single subject, full length, entirely inside the frame. The top edge of the frame sits about one fifth of the frame height above the crown of her hair, that space filled with plain backdrop. Her head, from the top of the hair to the point of the chin, measures about one sixth of the frame height, and her head is centred at about half the frame width, with her crouched body filling the middle and lower right of the picture. The bottom edge of the frame crosses the floor about one twentieth of the frame height below the toe of her forward shoe, so both shoes and the shadow beneath her are fully inside the picture. The telephone base sits on the floor at the lower left, its nearest edge about one fifth of the frame width in from the left edge and its top about one seventh of the frame height above the bottom edge. Her extended hand reaches out to the left and stops about one seventh of the frame width in from the left edge. The right edge of the frame leaves a margin of about one twelfth of the frame width beyond her outermost shoulder. Lens 70mm, camera level with her head in the crouched position and held perfectly level, no tilt, so the backdrop's fall to the floor stays horizontal. Aperture f/8.

POSE — She is in a deep crouch, balanced on the balls of both feet with both heels lifted clear of the floor. Both knees are bent well past ninety degrees so her thighs fold down against her calves and her hips sit low, just above her heels. Her knees are apart and both point toward the left of the frame, the near knee higher and further forward, the far knee lower and set back, so the two legs stack in depth rather than side by side. Her feet are placed one in front of the other: the forward foot is on the left of the frame with the toe pointed down and the heel raised, the rear foot on the right with its thin heel angled back and clear of the ground. Her torso is upright and vertical above the hips, rotated about twenty degrees toward camera left, her shoulders square and lifted slightly. Her head is upright, level, turned to face the camera almost frontally and tipped a few degrees toward her raised hand. Her eyes are aimed straight into the lens. Her right arm — on the right of the frame — is raised: the upper arm hangs close to her ribs, the elbow bends to about ninety degrees, and the forearm rises so the hand comes up beside her jaw. Her left arm — on the left of the frame — extends outward and slightly down in an unbroken line from shoulder to upper arm to elbow to forearm to wrist to hand, the elbow almost straight with only a soft bend, the arm held roughly horizontal at shoulder height so it reaches out across the empty left side of the frame.

HANDS AND CONTACT — The raised hand grips the handset around its slim middle bar: the fingers curl around the far side of the bar, the thumb lies along the near side, the index knuckle is highest, and the wrist is cocked slightly back so the earpiece of the handset presses against her ear and cheek while the mouthpiece angles down and away from her chin. The extended hand pinches the cord between the pad of the thumb and the side of the index finger, that pinch held about level with her shoulder; the middle, ring and little fingers are curled loosely into the palm, and the wrist is relaxed and turned so the back of the hand faces the camera.

EXPRESSION — Both brows are raised into curved arches, drawing two faint horizontal creases across the forehead. The eyes are open wide with a clear catchlight in each, the lower lids lifted a little by the cheeks. The cheeks are pushed up high, creasing at the outer corner of each eye. The mouth is open into a broad smile, the corners pulled up and back, the upper teeth showing across the full width and the lower lip curved down and relaxed with the tongue not visible. The fold running from each nostril to the corner of the mouth is deepened. The whole upper face moves with the mouth rather than staying still — this is delight, not a posed smile.

HAIR — The hair from image 1, worn long and loose in soft defined waves and curls, parted a little off centre, falling forward over both shoulders and down the back with plenty of volume at the sides. Individual curls are resolved at the outline against the backdrop, several strands standing free of the mass so the silhouette is textured rather than smooth. A few finer strands lie across the shoulder of the jacket. The near side of the hair falls partly across the raised forearm.

WARDROBE — An oversized black suit in a matte wool with a slightly hairy surface: the fibre absorbs light, so the cloth reads as a deep flat black and shows its shape only as a slight lift toward grey along the crest of each fold. The jacket is boxy and several sizes too large, its padded shoulder seams sitting well outboard of her actual shoulders, the armhole low, the sleeves long enough to reach the knuckles and gathering into three or four soft horizontal creases at the inside of each elbow. It has a notch lapel with a flat pressed edge that catches a thin line of light, a flapped hip pocket on the near side, and three small matte black buttons on each cuff. The jacket is worn open and its front panels hang loose, swinging out over the folded knees and breaking into thick angular folds where the crouch compresses them. Under it a crisp white cotton shirt: the collar shows as two small bright points at her throat and the cuff shows as a narrow white band at the wrist of the extended arm, and the white poplin is the brightest surface on her body, at least three stops above the wool. A narrow black satin tie hangs from the collar down the centre of her chest, and because the satin is a lustrous weave it lays one broad soft band of light along the length of the blade and goes dark at its edges, so the tie reads visibly glossier than the wool around it. Wide black wool trousers, loose and full through the thigh, pulling into long diagonal tension lines across the folded knees and gathering into deep soft folds at the ankle above the shoes. No pattern anywhere.

PROPS AND OBJECTS — A vintage push-button desk telephone in bright red, sitting flat on the floor. Its shell is hard injection-moulded plastic with a high gloss, so it behaves as a curved mirror: a long bright specular streak runs along the top edge of the body where the surface turns, a second broad soft reflection of the light source sits on the sloped front face, and the deepest part of the shell holds a dark reflection of the floor. Its keypad is a recessed rectangular panel of twelve small square black keys in a grid of four rows of three, each key slightly domed and returning a tiny highlight on its upper edge, set into a dark grey surround. A narrow row of vertical vents is moulded into the front skirt. Four small feet lift the body a few millimetres off the floor, so a tight dark contact shadow sits directly beneath it and a softer shadow spreads out behind it. The handset, in the same glossy red, is held to her ear: a rounded earpiece and mouthpiece joined by a slim flat bar, each end capped with a darker perforated disc. A black coiled cord connects them: it leaves the handset near her ear and runs across the frame to the left, pulled taut so its coils are stretched wide apart into a shallow regular wave that reads almost as a straight line, then, at her pinched fingers, it turns and drops down toward the floor as a long relaxed hanging coil with its loops close together and progressively looser as it nears the phone, finally curving in to plug into the back of the base. The cord is matte black rubber with a faint sheen along the top of each loop. Black pointed-toe slingback heels in a matte suede, with a thin strap crossing the instep fastened by a small silver buckle that returns one hard pinpoint of light, and a slim high stiletto heel; the suede absorbs light and reads as a soft flat black with no reflection.

LIGHTING — A single large soft source placed high and to camera left, well forward of the subject, angled down about forty degrees. Shadow edges are soft-cored but clearly placed: the brow drops a soft band onto the upper lids, the nose lays a short shadow down and to the right onto the cheek, the raised handset throws a soft shadow onto the jaw and neck below it, and the jacket's lapel casts a soft line across the shirt. The shadow side of her face sits about one and a half stops below the lit side and stays fully open. On the floor, a soft grey shadow of the whole crouched figure spreads to the right and slightly back, its edge progressively softer the further it travels; a second, smaller and darker contact shadow sits directly under the balls of both feet and under the telephone, anchoring them to the floor. The backdrop is brightest in a broad pool behind and to the left of her head and falls off toward the top corners and toward the right edge, ending about one and a half stops down. Every transition curves with the surface it crosses; nothing is straight-edged. The lighting sets brightness and falloff only.

BACKGROUND — A plain seamless studio backdrop in a light neutral grey, curving without a visible edge into a floor of the same material, so the wall-to-floor transition is a soft gradual bend rather than a line. The surface is matte and paper-like, with a very fine even tooth and no seam, texture, object or mark anywhere on it. Depth is carried by two things only: the luminance gradient across the backdrop, and the cast shadows lying on the floor.

FOCUS — Depth-of-field blur only, no motion blur anywhere; every edge is a still edge and the cord is not smeared. Everything on the subject is critically sharp: her eyes, the individual lashes, the iris texture and the pores along the cheekbone are all resolved, and so are the weave of the wool, the white shirt cuff, the buckle on the shoe and the keys on the telephone. The telephone and the shoes, being on the same floor plane and only slightly nearer the lens, stay sharp. The backdrop behind her is just off the plane of sharpness and reads smooth.

COLOUR — This is a grey, black and white picture with exactly one saturated colour in it. The backdrop and the floor are true neutral grey with no tint of any kind; the suit and the shoes are neutral black; the shirt is neutral white. Against those, the telephone and its handset are a single strong red, and they are the only chromatic objects in the frame — nothing else in the picture carries any hue except her skin, which stays warm and natural with red concentrated at the lips, the cheeks, the ears and the fingertips. The red of the phone must not bleed onto the floor or the backdrop around it. There is no blue, no green and no warm cast on the grey.

CAPTURE — A real exposure made on a full-frame camera in a studio. Light falls off slightly toward the four corners. The specular streak on the telephone shell and the point on the shoe buckle clip hard to white and stay very small; the brightest fold of the white shirt collar clips softly and keeps its shape rather than going flat. Shadows stay open — the black wool holds its fold structure and its weave rather than collapsing into a single flat mass, and the deepest value in the frame sits just above pure black. Skin tone varies across the face rather than running uniform: warmer and redder at the cheeks, the ears and the lower lip, cooler across the forehead, with a slight sheen on the nose and the top of the cheekbone. Pores, individual eyebrow hairs, single curls at the outline and the fine hairs on the back of the extended hand are all resolved. Very slight fine grain throughout, a little heavier in the darker areas of the backdrop.

FINAL CHECK — One adult woman, alone, in a deep crouch with both heels lifted, her whole body and both shoes inside the frame with floor visible beneath them, her head about one sixth of the frame height. The red telephone sits on the floor at the lower left, the coiled cord stretched taut and nearly straight between her pinched fingers and the handset at her ear, then dropping in a loose hanging coil down to the base. Do not stand her up and do not crop the shoes.

title: Retrato Moderno com Luzes Neon
description: Um retrato vibrante de um jovem estiloso com óculos e jaqueta puffer, em um cenário de luzes neon coloridas.
prompt:
SWAP SLOT — Image 1 is the identity reference. Take from it only the face, the skin tone, the hair colour and texture, and the head and body proportions of the person in this picture. THE PICTURE — A vertical night street-fashion portrait of one adult man, alone, in an oversized open puffer jacket over a rust knit sweater, shot from very low and very close with a wide lens, looking down into the camera, with long bands of warm ceiling light glowing out of focus behind him.

THE READING — This is a picture about presence and scale, and both are produced by physical facts rather than by mood. The camera is placed below his chest and tilted steeply up, so the viewer is looking up at him and he is looking down into the lens. Because the lens is wide and close, the jacket nearest the camera is rendered far larger than his head: the padded chest and shoulders become the widest and heaviest mass in the frame and the head sits small above them, which reads as monumentality, not as smallness. His head is tilted to one side, breaking the vertical of the body so the pose is not a stiff stack. His mouth is closed with one corner very slightly raised and the eyes are steady, so the face is unhurried rather than performing. Nothing in the body is working: the shoulders are down, the neck is loose, the whole figure is at rest inside a very large garment.

FRAMING AND CAMERA — Aspect ratio 4:5, vertical. The top edge of the frame passes just above the crown of his hair, leaving a gap of about one fiftieth of the frame height, so the head is pressed hard against the top of the picture. His head, from the top of the hair to the point of the chin, measures about three tenths of the frame height, and it is placed left of centre, its centre at about one third of the frame width. The remaining two thirds of the picture below and to the right of the head are filled almost entirely by the jacket. The left edge of the frame crosses the near front panel and sleeve of the jacket, which continue past the edge. The right edge crosses the large padded shoulder of the jacket, which also continues past the edge. The bottom edge crosses the sweater and the lower panels of the jacket at mid-torso, and his body continues past the bottom edge. Lens 24mm, camera positioned about level with his lower chest, very close to him, and tilted upward roughly twenty-five degrees, so the perspective is strongly exaggerated: the padded chest and shoulders are enlarged, the head is reduced, and the bands of light behind converge as they run toward the upper left corner.

POSE — He stands upright and square, his torso rotated only about fifteen degrees toward camera left, shoulders relaxed and dropped inside the jacket. His head is upright but tilted sideways toward his own right by about fifteen degrees, so the crown leans toward the left of the frame and the jaw angles toward the right, and it is turned a few degrees to face the camera almost frontally. His chin is lowered slightly. Because the camera is below him, his eyes are aimed downward into the lens, the gaze direct and unwavering, and the lower rims of the irises sit clear of the lower lids. Both arms hang down at his sides inside the jacket sleeves in an unbroken line from shoulder to upper arm to elbow, and both continue past the bottom edge of the frame. The neck is long and loose, the shoulders carrying no tension.

EXPRESSION — The brows sit level and untensed, with no crease in the forehead. The eyelids are open and steady, the lower lids soft, the eyes calm and fixed on the lens. The nostrils are relaxed. The lips are closed and lightly together, full and unpressed, with one corner of the mouth raised a fraction more than the other so the mouth is very slightly asymmetric. The cheeks are still and the jaw is loose and unclenched. Nothing in the face is straining; the whole expression is held rather than made.

HAIR — The hair from image 1, worn short at the sides and left longer on top, dry and loosely disordered, swept sideways and forward across the forehead in soft separate strands with a few lifting free at the crown and along the parting. Because the strongest light comes from behind, the loose strands at the top and side of the head are lit from within and read as bright individual filaments against the dark background, while the mass of the hair beneath them stays dark.

WARDROBE — An oversized puffer jacket, worn fully open, and its construction is the point. The shell is a smooth glossy ripstop nylon: the surface is close to satin, so it lays one broad soft band of light along the crest of each padded tube and drops dark into the stitched channel between them, and it also picks up and returns the colour of whatever light falls on it, so the same jacket reads cool on one side of the body and warm on the other. The quilting runs in wide horizontal tubes across the chest and shoulders, each tube inflated into a rounded cylinder with a soft round end where it meets the front opening, and each stitched seam puckers the nylon into a shallow ring of small radial creases. The collar is a thick padded funnel that stands up on its own around the back and sides of his neck, its two front ends rolling open and away from the throat. The front opening is edged on both sides by a metal coil zip: the tape is a narrow flat band and the metal teeth catch light as an uneven broken line of small hard pinpoints running the full length of each edge, brighter where the edge faces the light and dying out where it turns away. The whole garment is several sizes too big, so the shoulders sit far outboard of his actual shoulders and the whole mass leans away from his body. Under it, a heavy rust-orange knit sweater in a matte lambswool: the fibre scatters light so the surface reads soft and completely without sheen, the individual stitches visible as a fine regular texture across the chest, with a ribbed crew neckline whose raised ribs catch a thin line of light on each crest and go dark in each channel. The knit is smooth across the chest and gathers into a few soft horizontal folds low down.

PROPS AND OBJECTS — Rectangular glasses with thick matte black acetate frames and straight temple arms running back over the ear. The acetate is matte, so it holds only a faint soft sheen along the top of each rim rather than a hard highlight, and it reads as a solid black shape against the skin. The lenses are clear and untinted: his eyes, lashes and the lower edges of his brows are fully visible through them, and each lens carries one long narrow soft reflection running diagonally across its upper corner, picking up the warm light behind.

THE HERO EFFECT — The background bands. Above and behind him runs a long ceiling structure of parallel linear light fixtures, and because they are far outside the plane of sharpness they are rendered as broad glowing stripes rather than as objects. Each band is a soft-edged ribbon of warm yellow-white light with no defined boundary — it fades outward into the darker channel beside it over a wide gradient, and its core is bright enough to clip. The bands run diagonally from the upper left toward the right, converging slightly as they recede because of the wide lens, and they are not identical: they vary in width, in brightness and in how much they fade along their length, some interrupted where the structure crosses them, so the array is irregular rather than a repeating pattern. Between them sit darker channels of dull metallic surface holding a dim warm reflection. This blur is depth-of-field blur, not motion blur: the bands are soft in every direction at once, spread evenly around their own axis, and they must not read as streaks dragged in one direction by a moving camera. Around the brightest cores the light blooms outward into the darker areas beside them as a soft warm halation, and that bloom eats slightly into the outline of his hair and his shoulder where they cross in front of it.

LIGHTING — Two sources of opposite colour. The warm one is the ceiling structure itself: large, high and behind him, spilling forward so it lights the top and back of his head as a bright warm edge that varies in width and breaks where the hair parts, and it is the light that the near front panel of the jacket, the sweater and the far side of his face take. The cool one is a smaller source high and to camera right, in front of him: it lands on the large padded shoulder and the tubes on the right of the frame, on the raised collar, and skims across the near cheekbone and the frame of the glasses. Shadow edges are soft everywhere. His face is about a stop below the brightest jacket tubes and about two stops below the cores of the bands behind. The underside of each padded tube and each stitched channel sits deep in shadow, so the jacket is read entirely as an alternation of lit crests and dark grooves. The background is about a stop and a half brighter than his lit skin. Every transition curves with the surface it crosses; nothing is straight-edged. The lighting sets brightness and falloff only.

BACKGROUND — Physically, the underside of a large ceiling canopy: long linear light fixtures set into a ribbed metal soffit, running in parallel lines away from the camera, with darker metal channels and a structural beam crossing them in the upper right. All of it dissolved by defocus. Depth is carried by three separations at three different scales: the huge near jacket, his head and shoulders behind it, and the ceiling structure far beyond.

FOCUS — Depth-of-field blur only. Critical sharpness sits on his eyes, seen through the clear lenses — the lashes, the iris texture and the fine skin beside the eye are resolved — and on the frame of the glasses and the bridge of the nose. The plane of sharpness carries the whole face and the front strands of hair. The raised collar and the nearest padded tubes, being closer to the lens, are slightly softer, the nylon's texture beginning to smooth while the shape of each tube stays fully readable. The large shoulder on the right of the frame is softer still. The ceiling bands are dissolved completely. Nothing in the picture is motion-blurred; every edge is a still edge.

COLOUR — Two opposed families and nothing else. The warm family is amber, orange and rust: the ceiling bands, the sweater, the near front panel of the jacket, and the warm edge on the hair. The cool family is cyan and pale blue-green: the large shoulder of the jacket, the raised collar and the light skimming the cheekbone. The two must stay separate and saturated, meeting on the jacket itself where one panel is cool and the other warm. There is no green, no magenta and no pure neutral grey anywhere in the frame. His skin holds its own tone between the two rather than tipping fully into either — warm at the ear, the nostril and the lips, cooler along the cheekbone where the cool source skims it, and never turning blue or turning orange.

CAPTURE — A real exposure made handheld at night on a full-frame camera at high ISO. Light falls off toward the four corners. FINAL CHECK — One adult man, alone. Camera low and close with a wide lens, tilted up, so his eyes look down into it and the jacket is much larger than his head; his head sits in the upper left third of the frame, about three tenths of the frame height, pressed close to the top edge, with the jacket filling everything below and to the right. THE READING — This is a portrait of authority, and authority is carried here by physical facts, not by mood. Every one of the following must be present, because together they are what produce it. title: Homem jogando xadrez com foco e estratégia

prompt:

THE PICTURE — A vertical outdoor editorial portrait of one adult man, alone, photographed on a city rooftop from a very low camera position just above the surface of a chessboard, so that the chess pieces stand large in the foreground and the man sits behind them against open sky.

FRAMING AND CAMERA — Aspect ratio 4:5, vertical. Single subject, centred horizontally with his head very slightly left of centre. The bottom edge of the frame crosses the near rank of the chessboard, so the board's near squares and the bases of the two closest pieces run along the bottom of the picture. The top edge sits about one eighth of the frame height above the top of his head, that gap filled with sky. The man's head measures about one seventh of the frame height. The left and right edges cross his shoulders and the outer edge of the board on each side; his shoulders continue past both edges. Lens 24mm, camera held about 30cm above the rooftop surface and tilted very slightly upward, so the perspective is strongly exaggerated: the chess pieces nearest the lens are rendered much larger than the man's head, his forward-reaching hand is rendered larger than his face, and the vertical lines of the background lean outward toward the corners. Aperture f/4.

POSE — He is crouched low behind the board, his weight settled back over his heels and his knees wide, his torso folded slightly forward from the hips so his chest leans over the far edge of the board. His shoulders are square to the camera. His near arm — the one on the left of the picture — extends forward and down across the board in an unbroken line from shoulder to upper arm to elbow to forearm to wrist to hand; the elbow is bent about thirty degrees and hangs just clear of the board's surface. That hand is closed in a pinch: thumb on the near side and the pads of the index and middle fingers on the far side of a tall light-wood queen at the front-left of the board, gripping the piece at the narrow neck just under its crown, the remaining two fingers curled loosely below. The tendons on the back of that hand stand up under the skin. His other arm reaches down on the right side of the picture, forearm angled inward, and the fingertips of that hand rest flat and spread on the board's far right corner, taking a little of his weight. His head is level and turned straight at the camera, chin held a fraction down so he is looking very slightly along his cheekbones. His eyes are aimed directly into the lens.

EXPRESSION — The brows sit low and level with a single shallow vertical crease between them. The eyelids are narrowed a little against the bright sun, the lower lids firm, the eyes steady and unblinking. The nostrils are relaxed. The lips are closed and pressed lightly together with the corners neither raised nor pulled down. The jaw is set, so the muscle at the back of the jaw shows faintly under the skin at the ear. The cheeks are still.

HAIR — The hair from image 1, worn short and swept back from the forehead, dry and slightly disordered by the wind, with individual strands lifting free at the crown and along the hairline and catching the sun as bright separate filaments. Short even stubble along the jaw, chin and upper lip, each hair casting its own small shadow.

WARDROBE — An unbuttoned camel wool overcoat in a coarse brushed weave: the fibre scatters the light so the fabric reads matte and slightly hazy at its edges, with no sheen anywhere, and the sunlit shoulders read as pale sand while the folds inside the lapels drop to a deep warm brown. The coat is open, the two front panels falling away from his chest and bunching into thick vertical folds where they compress against his bent thighs. The collar stands part way up at the back of his neck. Under it, a plain black shirt in a fine matte knit, buttoned to the second button, which absorbs the light and holds almost no detail in its folds beyond a faint grey along the crest of each. A slim silver curb chain lies against the exposed skin at the base of his throat, each link returning a small hard white pinpoint where it faces the sun and going dark grey on its underside. Dark charcoal trousers, visible only where his thighs press against the inside of the open coat. No pattern anywhere on any garment.

PROPS AND OBJECTS — A wooden chessboard rests flat on the rooftop between him and the camera, filling the lower third of the frame and running out past both side edges. Its squares are polished light maple and dark walnut, the grain visible in the pale squares, the lacquer returning a broad soft reflection of the sky across the near squares and a hard white streak where the sun strikes the board's edge. The pieces are turned wood in the same two tones: cream and dark brown, with visible lathe rings around their bases and the small chips and worn edges of a set that has been used. Because of the low camera, the two pieces nearest the lens — a cream queen at front left, held in his fingers, and a dark bishop at front right — stand tall in the frame, their tops rising above the level of his shoulders, their forms slightly stretched by the wide lens. Six or seven further pieces are scattered across the board in a plausible mid-game arrangement, each smaller than the last as the board recedes, and each casting a short hard-edged shadow that falls back and to the right across the squares. The cream wood takes the sun and shows a soft graduated shading around each turned curve; the dark wood holds a narrow bright highlight along its lit side and goes nearly black on the shadow side.

LIGHTING — A single small hard source high and slightly in front of the subject, a little to camera left: direct midday sun in a clear sky. Shadow edges are crisp with almost no gradation — the nose lays a short defined shadow down and to the right onto the upper lip, the brow ridge puts a distinct band of shadow across the upper eyelids, and the chin drops a hard shadow onto the neck. The eye sockets stay open and readable rather than blocking up, filled by light bouncing back off the pale rooftop and the board. The ratio between the lit side of his face and the shadow side is about three stops. Every piece on the board and every fold of the coat throws its own separate hard shadow in the same direction. The background is roughly one stop brighter than his lit skin. Every shadow transition curves with the surface it crosses; nothing is straight-edged.

BACKGROUND — Behind him, deep saturated blue sky occupying most of the upper frame, with three or four scattered cumulus clouds of unequal size — one larger and low near his right shoulder, two smaller and higher — each with a bright crisp upper edge and a slightly grey flat base, none of them symmetrical. Across the lower part of the sky runs a horizontal metal roof-edge railing, galvanised grey, its top rail passing behind him at about the level of his chest, the uprights spaced evenly and leaning outward toward the frame corners under the wide lens. To the right and set back, a small square metal chimney vent with a capped top, weathered and streaked. The rooftop surface itself is pale grey mineral membrane with a fine gritty texture, running from the bottom corners of the frame away to the railing, with a faint seam line crossing it. Depth is carried by three separations: the near pieces, the man and the railing behind him, and the sky beyond.

FOCUS — Depth-of-field blur only, no motion blur anywhere; every edge in the picture is a still edge. Critical sharpness sits on his eyes and the bridge of his nose — individual lashes and the fine texture of the iris are resolved. The plane of sharpness carries his face, his chain and the front of his coat. His forward hand, being closer to the lens, is a little softer, with the skin texture just beginning to lose definition. The two large foreground pieces are noticeably out of focus, their outlines soft and their surfaces smooth, but their shapes remain fully readable. The railing and the chimney vent behind him are slightly soft. The clouds are soft.

COLOUR — A three-colour picture: saturated blue sky, warm camel and cream woods, and black. The blue is deep and clean with no cyan cast. The warm tones are all in the yellow-brown range and never drift pink. The greys of the rooftop and the railing stay genuinely neutral, so the warm and the cool sit against each other without either bleeding into the other. There is no green anywhere.

CAPTURE — A real exposure made on a full-frame camera in direct sun. Light falls off slightly toward the four corners. The brightest specular points on the chain and the board's lacquer clip hard to white and small; the sunlit cloud edges clip softly and hold a trace of shape. Shadows stay open and detailed rather than crushing to black. Skin tone varies across his face — redder at the nostrils, ears and the edges of the fingers, cooler and paler across the forehead — and pores, the fine hairs on the back of the hand and the individual stubble hairs are resolved. Very slight fine grain throughout, heavier in the shadow areas. The three distance planes sit at three visibly different degrees of focus.

FINAL CHECK — One adult man, alone. Camera down at board level, the bottom edge crossing the near rank of the chessboard and the foreground pieces standing tall and out of focus in the lower third of the frame; his head no more than one seventh of the frame height, with sky above it. Do not raise the camera and do not widen the shot.

O vetor ocular é direto e frontal, com as pupilas alinhadas coaxialmente ao centro óptico da lente. Não há desvio binocular, sugerindo um foco intenso e direto no ponto de captura.

**[Hand/Object Tactile Interaction]**
A mão direita do sujeito está em contato físico com a lapela do paletó. Os dedos médio, anelar e mínimo estão flexionados, agarrando firmemente o tecido. O polegar está estendido e repousa na parte interna da lapela, enquanto o indicador está levemente fletido e posicionado sobre a borda externa da lapela. Há uma deformação dérmica visível nas pontas dos dedos e na palma da mão devido à pressão exercida sobre o tecido, indicando um contato tátil significativo. A hierarquia de oclusão (Z-depth) é: Pele (dedos) > Tecido (lapela) > Pele (punho/braço coberto).

**[Subject (Anonymous)]**
Retrato de um indivíduo em postura confiante, com expressão contemplativa e engajada.

**[New Clothing Design]**
Um blazer casual, confeccionado em tecido de lã penteada cor areia, com uma textura sutil de espinha de peixe (herringbone pattern) e um BxDF que simula a suavidade da lã com um leve brilho acetinado sob a luz direta. O corte é slim-fit, com lapelas entalhadas e um único botão frontal. Uma única fenda traseira garante mobilidade. O design mantém a simplicidade e elegância, adaptando o material para uma sensação mais luxuosa e tátil.

**[Background & Layout]**
Fundo neutro, completamente preto, simulando um vácuo fotônico onde nenhuma luz residual é detectada. A composição é centralizada, com o sujeito ocupando aproximadamente 70% do quadro verticalmente e 60% horizontalmente. Não há elementos distrativos ou linhas de guia além do próprio sujeito.

**[Physics of Light]**
Uma única fonte de luz principal (key light) posicionada à direita e ligeiramente acima da câmera (aproximadamente 45 graus de ângulo horizontal e 20 graus de ângulo vertical em relação ao sujeito). Há "black clipping" extremo nas áreas mais profundas das sombras, especialmente no lado esquerdo do corpo e no fundo, onde se assume "Zero Fill Light" e "100% Shadow Opacity" para emular o mais puro silêncio fotônico. Os destaques são suaves, sem hot spots, sugerindo um difusor ou softbox na fonte de luz. A luz lateral realça a textura do cabelo, barba e da lapela do paletó.

**[Bio-Dermal Texture]**
A pele exibe um modelo de 3-layer SSS (Subsurface Scattering) nos áreas iluminadas, revelando a translucidez da derme e epiderme. Um micro-displacement sutil é aplicado para replicar poros finos e as linhas de expressão mais suaves apenas nas regiões diretamente atingidas pela luz, evitando qualquer detalhe em áreas de sombra total para manter o contraste dramático. A textura da barba é replicada com strand-based hair, com variação de cor e espessura para um realismo aprimorado.

**[Sony A1 Setup]**

title: Marçal
prompt:
[Camera Angle/Pitch]**
Low-Angle Medium Shot. Altura da câmera calibrada para 1.05m do chão virtual. Ângulo de pitch de +5 graus (levemente para cima), focalizando o centro do rosto e o entrelaçamento das mãos. Distância focal equivalente a 85mm.

**[Body-to-Head Torque]**
O tronco do sujeito está ligeiramente rotacionado em -5 graus (para a direita do observador) em relação ao plano da câmera. O rosto, no entanto, está rotacionado em +2 graus (para a esquerda do observador), alinhando o olhar diretamente com a lente. Essa micro-rotação induz um torque cinesiologicamente perceptível no pescoço, indicando uma tensão controlada nos músculos esternocleidomastóideo e trapézio, expressando uma postura de atenção concentrada. O alinhamento dos ombros é aproximadamente paralelo ao plano horizontal da imagem.

**[Gaze Vector]**
O vetor ocular é um alinhamento direto da pupila com o centro óptico da lente. A íris está concentricamente posicionada na pupila, com um vetor de olhar que denota atenção fixa e penetrante. Não há desvio paralático, indicando uma fixação direta no ponto de observação. As pálpebras estão abertas em 85% da abertura máxima, sem indicar fadiga ou relaxamento excessivo, mas sim uma vigilância calculada.

**[Hand/Object Tactile Interaction]**
As mãos estão em contato interdigital, formando uma estrutura de suporte para a cabeça (embora a cabeça não esteja apoiada). A mão esquerda superior se sobrepõe à mão direita inferior.
*   **Oclusão (Z-Depth):** A mão esquerda (superior) oclui completamente a porção distal dos dedos da mão direita. A porção proximal dos dedos da mão direita é ocluída parcialmente pelos dedos da mão esquerda.
*   **Dermal Deformation:** Há uma compressão mínima nos pontos de contato entre os dedos, visível como um leve achatamento das almofadas digitais e uma reconfiguração sutil das linhas de flexão. A pressão é controlada, sem indicação de esforço excessivo. A pele dos nós dos dedos superiores apresenta micro-rugas devido à flexão. Um anel metálico (ouro fosco, 24k, largura de 3mm, perfil retangular com bordas suavizadas) está posicionado no dedo anelar da mão esquerda, sem causar deformação dérmica significativa, apenas uma leve indentação superficial que segue a geometria do anel.

**[Subject (Anonymous)]**
Indivíduo de constituição atlética, postura ereta, com vestimenta formal.

**[New Clothing Design]**
O sujeito veste um traje formal de três peças, confeccionado em lã virgem super 150s na cor grafite escuro (quase preto).
*   **Blazer:** Lapela notch de 8cm de largura, fechamento frontal de dois botões de chifre escuro, com bolsos de lapela com aba. Mangas com quatro botões funcionais em um "kissing stack". O corte é slim fit, mas com amplitude suficiente para movimentos controlados. Forro em seda jacquard tom sobre tom.
*   **Camisa:** Tecido de algodão Pima 120s/2, weave espinha de peixe (herringbone), cor carvão. Colarinho spread com baleias removíveis, punhos franceses (double cuffs) com abotoaduras discretas em ônix.
*   **Coletes:** Colete de seis botões, com bolsos embutidos e ajustador traseiro, em tecido idêntico ao blazer.

**[Background & Layout]**
O fundo é uma composição dinâmica de elementos abstratos em explosão. A porção superior esquerda e superior direita são dominadas por nuvens de fumaça densa e escombros que se dissipam em tons de cinza escuro a quase preto. No centro do fundo, atrás do sujeito, uma explosão de fogo irradia chamas laranjas e vermelhas intensas, com partículas incandescentes e fragmentos projetados para fora, criando um senso de caos controlado. Integrados à composição do fundo, elementos gráficos de notas de moeda (especificamente, uma nota de 100 unidades monetárias com um retrato presidencial) aparecem parcialmente queimadas e desintegrando-se, com a figura do retrato desbotada e em tom sépia, imersa nas chamas. Um olho aparece como um elemento sutil, translúcido, na parte superior direita do fundo, observando a cena de forma enigmática.

**[Physics of Light]**
Iluminação principal (Key Light) a 45 graus superior direita, um softbox retangular de 120x90cm com grid, temperatura de cor de 5600K, intensidade de 8000 lumens, gerando um contraste dramático no lado esquerdo do rosto do sujeito.
*   **Fill Light:** Um softbox octogonal de 90cm a 30 graus superior esquerda, 5600K, 2000 lumens, com difusor pesado, suavizando sombras no lado esquerdo.
*   **Backlight/Rim Light:** Duas tiras de LED RGBW posicionadas atrás e acima dos ombros do sujeito, emitindo um brilho sutil de cor laranja/vermelho (aproximando-se das cores do fogo no fundo), com intensidade de 1500 lumens cada, criando um contorno definido e separando o sujeito do fundo.
*   **Black Clipping:** As áreas mais profundas das dobras do traje e as áreas de sombra total sob o queixo e nos cotovelos apresentam black clipping acentuado, simulando uma absorção de luz quase completa.
*   **Zero Fill Light:** As sombras projetadas por objetos no fundo (como as notas queimando) e as sombras intrínsecas ao fogo (onde a luz não penetra totalmente) exibem zero fill light e 100% de opacidade, resultando em áreas de escuridão absoluta.

**[Bio-Dermal Texture]**
A pele do rosto e das mãos apresenta um SSS (Subsurface Scattering) de 3 camadas (epiderme, derme, gordura subcutânea), visível nas áreas onde a luz principal e de preenchimento incide. Micro-displacement mapeado para realçar os poros e a textura fina da pele nas regiões iluminadas do nariz, maçãs do rosto e na parte superior dos nós dos dedos. Capilares subcutâneos são sutilmente visíveis na derme superficial, especialmente nas regiões com menor espessura de pele. O cabelo e a barba apresentam micro-filamentos individuais com um shader anisotrópico para simular o brilho direcional.

**[Sony A1 Setup]**
*   **Camera Model:** Sony Alpha 1
*   **Lens:** Sony FE 85mm f/1.4 GM
*   **Aperture:** f/4.0 (para um equilíbrio entre profundidade de campo e separação do fundo)
*   **Shutter Speed:** 1/200 sec (para congelar qualquer movimento sutil e sincronizar com flashes)
*   **ISO:** 200 (para máxima qualidade de imagem e mínimo ruído)
*   **White Balance:** Custom, calibrado para 5600K.
*   **Metering Mode:** Spot Metering (na parte mais brilhante do rosto)
*   **Focus Mode:** Continuous AF (AF-C) com Eye-AF ativado.
*   **Picture Profile:** S-Log3 (para máxima latitude dinâmica, pós-produção)
*   **Color Space:** S-Gamut3.Cine
*   **Resolution:** 8640 x 5760 pixels (Full Frame)

**[Negative Instructions]**
- Evitar tons de pele excessivamente saturados ou desaturados.
- Não incluir texto ou logotipos na imagem final.
- Não introduzir elementos de humor ou ironia.
- Não distorcer as proporções anatômicas do sujeito.
- Não permitir que as chamas ou elementos do fundo ocluem significativamente as feições do sujeito.
- Não utilizar fontes de luz dura que criem sombras muito nítidas ou dramáticas no rosto, exceto onde intencional para aumentar o contraste.
- Não alterar a expressão facial para algo além de concentrada e séria.

title: thumbnail
prompt:
Imagem de estudo e concentração com uma pessoa sentada em uma mesa, escrevendo em um livro aberto, ladeada por pilhas de livros. O fundo apresenta uma multidão desfocada dividida por iluminação contrastante, e um elemento de texto flutuante acima da cabeça do sujeito.

[Camera Angle/Pitch] Medium Shot, eye-level perspective, positioned directly in front of the subject. Camera height is approximately 1.65m from the floor, aligning with the subject's eye line. Pitch angle is precisely 0 degrees, maintaining a perfectly horizontal sightline. The focal length simulates an 85mm lens on a full-frame sensor, providing a natural compression and shallow depth of field.

[Body-to-Head Torque] O tronco do sujeito está alinhado frontalmente com a mesa e o eixo da câmera, com rotação de 0 graus. A cabeça está centralizada e ereta, sem rotação lateral ou inclinação, resultando em 0 graus de torque cervical rotacional. A musculatura do pescoço (esternocleidomastoideo, trapézio superior) está em tensão isométrica para manter a postura, indicando foco e estabilidade, sem sinais de fadiga ou esforço excessivo. Os ombros estão ligeiramente elevados e retraídos, sugerindo uma postura engajada.

[Gaze Vector] O vetor ocular é direto e inabalável, com as pupilas perfeitamente centradas nas íris e alinhadas com o eixo óptico da lente da câmera. A geometria da pupila é circular e simétrica, refletindo uma fixação visual precisa no ponto de observação.

[Hand/Object Tactile Interaction] A mão direita do sujeito (do ponto de vista do observador) segura um instrumento de escrita. Os dedos (polegar, indicador e médio) aplicam pressão controlada, resultando em deformação dérmica sutil nas pontas dos dedos e na base do polegar, onde a pele se molda ao contorno do instrumento. O instrumento faz contato direto com a superfície do papel no livro aberto, com o papel ligeiramente comprimido sob a ponta. A mão esquerda repousa plana sobre a página esquerda do livro aberto, com os dedos ligeiramente afastados. A deformação dérmica é mínima, consistindo em um leve achatamento das almofadas dos dedos contra a superfície do papel, indicando um contato suave para estabilizar o livro. A hierarquia de oclusão é: Instrumento de Escrita > Dedos (mão direita) > Papel > Livro; e Dedos (mão esquerda) > Papel > Livro.

[Subject (Anonymous)] Um indivíduo em estado de concentração intensa, engajado em uma atividade de estudo ou escrita.

[New Clothing Design] Um moletom de gola redonda oversized, confeccionado em malha de algodão orgânico de alta gramatura (loopback terry), na cor cinza neutro e desaturado. O design apresenta ombros caídos (dropped shoulders), punhos e gola canelados de largura generosa, e uma bainha ligeiramente mais curta e reta. A textura do tecido deve ser visivelmente irregular, com as alças do loopback terry evidentes, conferindo um BxDF difuso com micro-rugosidade e absorção de luz. Sem capuz, sem cordões, sem bolsos frontais.

[Background & Layout] O fundo é dividido em duas zonas distintas. À esquerda, uma multidão de figuras humanas desfocadas e desaturadas, imersas em uma atmosfera fria e escura, sugerindo um ambiente de massa ou indiferença. À direita, uma multidão similar, mas banhada por uma luz quente e avermelhada, evocando uma sensação de urgência ou intensidade. Ambas as multidões são renderizadas com um desfoque gaussiano profundo (aproximadamente f/2.0 de profundidade de campo), tornando as figuras indistinguíveis. Na mesa, pilhas de livros antigos e encadernados em couro ou tecido escuro flanqueiam o sujeito, criando uma moldura simétrica. À esquerda, um conjunto de marcadores coloridos (amarelo, laranja, verde) dispostos horizontalmente. À direita, um copo de vidro transparente com água, exibindo refrações sutis. O texto flutuante "[TEXTO AQUI]" é posicionado centralmente acima da cabeça do sujeito, em uma fonte sans-serif bold, com uma cor dourada-alaranjada emissiva e um halo de luz.

[Physics of Light] A iluminação principal é um softbox grande e difuso, posicionado ligeiramente acima e à frente do sujeito, criando uma luz suave e uniforme no rosto e parte superior do corpo. Uma luz de contorno (rim light) quente e intensa emana da direita, acentuando o cabelo e o ombro direito do sujeito. Uma luz de contorno mais fria e sutil ilumina o lado esquerdo. O fundo esquerdo exibe black clipping significativo nas sombras mais profundas da multidão, com 100% de opacidade de sombra e zero fill light. O fundo direito, embora iluminado por uma fonte quente, também apresenta áreas de black clipping nas sombras da multidão. O texto "[TEXTO AQUI]" atua como uma fonte de luz emissiva, projetando um brilho dourado-alaranjado que interage com o cabelo e a testa do sujeito. Reflexos especulares mínimos são visíveis na superfície da mesa e no copo d'água.

[Bio-Dermal Texture] Aplicação de SSS (Subsurface Scattering) de 3 camadas em todas as áreas expostas da pele (rosto, pescoço, mãos) onde a luz incide diretamente, simulando a dispersão da luz sob a superfície dérmica para um realismo translúcido. Micro-displacement é aplicado para renderizar poros finos, linhas de expressão sutis e variações texturais microscópicas, especialmente visíveis na testa, sob os olhos e nas articulações dos dedos, sem exagerar as características. O cabelo é renderizado com fios individuais, sombreamento anisotrópico e um SSS sutil para capturar a textura natural e a interação da luz.

    *   **Luz de Contorno (Direita):** Strobe nu com gel CTO completo, posicionado à direita da câmera e atrás do sujeito, mirando o lado direito da cabeça e ombro. Potência: 1/8.
    *   **Luz de Contorno (Esquerda):** Strobe nu com gel 1/4 CTB, posicionado à esquerda da câmera e atrás do sujeito, mirando o lado esquerdo da cabeça e ombro. Potência: 1/16.
